2+ years of experience in data science with a proven track record of delivering impactful data-driven solutions, a strong background in AI/ML, and familiarity with modern software development processes
Strong technical skills, including proficiency in statistical analysis, deep learning methods, and AI/ML frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch
Experience with AI/ML deployment, Python programming, data analysis, data manipulation, signal processing and visualization tools
A degree in Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field - or equivalent work experience
Familiarity with Linux environments and containerization tools such as Docker
Experience with Java is an advantage but not a requirement
Most importantly, genuine passion and creativity - if you have fun side projects, unconventional experiences, or unique perspectives, we would love to hear about them

We value our colleagues and our meaningful contributions to securing people through advanced technology. You will also experience that we have a strong focus on your development, teaching you useful new competences and further strengthening current ones, both professionally and personally. Our company culture is autonomous and engaging, and we acknowledge the importance of flexibility in a great working environment.

When joining Terma, we promise that you will experience: Great people, challenging tasks, world-class expertise, and meaningful contribution in your daily work.

At Terma, we prioritize the well-being of our employees, ensuring they are well taken care of. Joining our team comes with a multitude of perks designed to enhance your social life, cultural experiences, and health.

International Environment: Explore great teamwork and professional sparring with colleagues around the world.

Well-being Perks: Opportunity to enroll in our on-site massage-offer at our locations in Denmark.

Competence networking across professional experts in Terma: Professional presentations and knowledge sharing across the organization.

Our commitment to DEIB (Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging) means we actively value and celebrate unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. We strive to create an environment where all employees have equal opportunities to succeed, feel respected and valued, and experience a true sense of belonging.

To ensure that your application will reach us and is properly processed, we only accept applications via www.terma.com. Applications will be processed continuously.

Lystrup: KEPA@terma.com

Søborg: DANO@terma.com

Are you passionate about AI, eager to make a real impact, and ready to work on solutions that truly matter? Would you like the opportunity to tackle exciting challenges, shape the future of advanced AI technologies, and make a meaningful difference? Then this opportunity is for you!

We are facing an exciting future with considerable growth and demanding changes, as we deliver advanced technologies and mission critical solutions for the defense and aerospace industry. Our systems provide security for people on land, at sea and in the air. Therefore, we are looking for a Data Scientist to become part of this journey and contribute to our overall purpose – securing people through advanced technology.

Your role in our team

As a Data Scientist in AI & Advanced Analytics, you will play a pivotal role in developing advanced AI capabilities that directly support critical defense operations. Working with complex, real-world data and mission-driven challenges, you will help shape the next generation of intelligent systems used by Denmark and our international partners. You will:

Build state-of-the-art AI capabilities – Work with untamed data, train deep learning models, and evaluate them to ensure top-tier quality and generalization. A strong foundation in statistics and mathematics is essential, along with the ability to apply new deep learning techniques and architectures.

Take ownership of AI and data modeling for key projects – Develop AI models for impactful projects in collaboration with a talented team, solving a wide range of real-world challenges.

Ensure top-tier quality and security – Handle classified information and mission-critical systems while adhering to military-grade security standards.

Collaborate and engage with end users – Work closely with stakeholders to ensure AI solutions meet operational needs, delivering real-world impact.

Since early 2022, the global security landscape has changed significantly. Denmark and its NATO allies face increasingly complex challenges that require rapid, innovative technological responses. Within Terma’s AI & Advanced Analytics team, we develop and deploy AI-driven capabilities that strengthen decision-making and enhance situational awareness in this evolving environment.

We are a passionate and dedicated group that takes full ownership of our AI products – from initial ideas to development, delivery, and long-term maintenance. Our work extends far beyond coding; we engage directly with customers and end users to understand operational needs and ensure that our solutions make a real difference. This means you will work closely with those who rely on our technology, gaining unique insights that go well beyond the traditional developer role.

You will join a team that values innovation, diversity, and psychological safety. We support each other, challenge ideas constructively and ensure everyone has the opportunity to grow and contribute to delivering meaningful solutions.

How you will make a meaningful contribution

Your key responsibilities include:

    • Developing and training cutting-edge Machine learning models using complex, real-world and simulated data
    • Taking ownership of data pipelines, AI modeling, and algorithm development for high-impact projects
    • Ensuring high-quality, secure, and reliable AI solutions that meet military-grade standards
    • Evaluating model performance and driving continuous improvements in accuracy, robustness, and generalization
    • Collaborating closely with end users to understand operational needs and translate them into effective AI solutions
    • Working with peers across engineering, domain experts, and customers to deliver mission-critical capabilities

Bring your world class expertise into play

You are fluent in English both in writing and verbal at a professional level. Danish is an advantage but not a requirement. Moreover, we are also looking for a new colleague who has:

    • 2+ years of experience in data science with a proven track record of delivering impactful data-driven solutions, a strong background in AI/ML, and familiarity with modern software development processes
    • Strong technical skills, including proficiency in statistical analysis, deep learning methods, and AI/ML frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch
    • Experience with AI/ML deployment, Python programming, data analysis, data manipulation, signal processing and visualization tools
    • A degree in Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field - or equivalent work experience
    • Familiarity with Linux environments and containerization tools such as Docker
    • Experience with Java is an advantage but not a requirement
    • Most importantly, genuine passion and creativity - if you have fun side projects, unconventional experiences, or unique perspectives, we would love to hear about them

As a person, you are creative, and you believe in teamwork and thrive in an environment built on mutual trust and collaboration. We challenge ourselves and one another through sparring and collaboration. We have a team of friendly and welcoming people, and we expect you to fit this description as well. Being successful is a team effort. We have built our team on mutual trust in each other’s expertise and an informal cooperative culture. We all understand what role we play in keeping Denmark safe and are motivated by the impact we can make individually and particularly as a team.

We are an international company representing world-class expertise, delivering complex and high-tech products. We value our colleagues and our meaningful contributions to securing people through advanced technology. You will also experience that we have a strong focus on your development, teaching you useful new competences and further strengthening current ones, both professionally and personally. Our company culture is autonomous and engaging, and we acknowledge the importance of flexibility in a great working environment.

When joining Terma, we promise that you will experience: Great people, challenging tasks, world-class expertise, and meaningful contribution in your daily work.

Benefits at Terma

At Terma, we prioritize the well-being of our employees, ensuring they are well taken care of. Joining our team comes with a multitude of perks designed to enhance your social life, cultural experiences, and health.

International Environment: Explore great teamwork and professional sparring with colleagues around the world.
Flexible Working Hours: Enjoy the opportunity to work flexibly and the option to work from home up to two days per week. Internet connection at home is paid for by Terma.
Comprehensive Benefits Package: Receive a 10% paid pension along with a beneficial health care and insurance package. Enjoy discounts from various business partners.
Well-being Perks: Opportunity to enroll in our on-site massage-offer at our locations in Denmark.
Social and Professional Events: We have an active staff association that arranges a variety of social activities and events to bring all of our colleagues together
Competence networking across professional experts in Terma: Professional presentations and knowledge sharing across the organization.

We are dedicated to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and welcoming workplace. Our commitment to DEIB (Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging) means we actively value and celebrate unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. We strive to create an environment where all employees have equal opportunities to succeed, feel respected and valued, and experience a true sense of belonging.

To support an unbiased evaluation process, we kindly encourage applicants to omit personal details such as photos and age from their applications.

If you would like to take on the challenge of working in an innovative company, we look forward to receiving your application. A resume is required, while a cover letter is optional. To ensure that your application will reach us and is properly processed, we only accept applications via www.terma.com. Applications will be processed continuously.

Do you have any questions regarding the position?

Feel free to contact Hiring Manager on e-mail:

Lystrup: KEPA@terma.com

Søborg: DANO@terma.com

Bear in mind, that we need you to confirm that you can obtain a security clearance by the Danish Defense Intelligence Service, and that all adults in your household are not posing any risk to the related risk-evaluation. This entails among other issues:

    • That you have as a minimum stayed within NATO/EU/MISWG countries for the last 7 years only interrupted by short stays abroad, and
    • That you have not committed serious criminal offences

Title: Data Scientist
Description:
Banking hasn't changed much in decades. We're changing that. One product at a time.

Lunar is a Nordic challenger bank building the future of financial life with AI at the core. Our engineers, designers, and product people work on problems that actually matter. Making money simpler, smarter, and more rewarding for millions of people across the Nordics.

Fully licensed and founded in 2015, with offices in Copenhagen, Aarhus and Stockholm.




We move fast, we build with purpose, and we're just getting started.




As our new (Senior) Data Scientist you'll join our team based in Aarhus, reporting to Eugene, our Senior Engineering Manager, working to bring data and machine learning into how we prevent fraud, manage risk, and grow the business.




What will you do?

Design, build, and deploy machine learning and statistical models across fraud detection, transaction monitoring, loan risk assessment, customer risk scoring, and sales and lead generation
Build and operate experimentation and evaluation frameworks — using tools like MLflow and Metaflow — with strong test sets and benchmarks across projects
Dive into data analysis and feature engineering to keep pushing model performance further
Partner closely with data engineers, analysts, and business stakeholders to define requirements and turn insight into decisions
Document models, methodologies, and results clearly, and bring the latest ML and GenAI advances into how Lunar builds




What are we looking for in you?

Experience developing and deploying machine learning models in a production environment
Proficiency in Python and relevant ML libraries (e.g., scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch)
Experience with cloud-based ML platforms such as AWS SageMaker or Kubeflow
Solid grounding in machine learning, statistical modeling, and data analysis techniques — experience in financial services or another regulated industry is a plus
Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into business insight




Benefits and perks

4 days in the office. We're a team that builds together, thinks together, and moves together. Showing up is part of how we work.
State of the art equipment. The newest computer, monitor, mouse, and keyboard. We want you to do your best work without anything slowing you down.
Pension, health insurance, and enhanced parental leave. From your financial future to your family moments. We've got you covered.




Are you ready to join the journey? Apply now and let's find out more!

Title: Lead Data Scientist, Commercialisation AI
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Looking to turn data and AI into real commercial impact? Join us to build the solutions shaping how Lundbeck makes commercial decisions.

You will be the technical anchor and hands-on builder for AI/ML solutions that shape commercial decisions at Lundbeck: from forecasting and causal inference to GenAI assistants and agentic workflows. If you like taking a model from prototype to production and working shoulder to shoulder with the people who use it, read on.

You’ll join our newly established Data, Insights and AI team in Global Customer Experience (GCX), helping build and scale advanced analytics, ML and AI across the commercial organisation. As Lead Data Scientist, you’ll design and build end-to-end solutions, including econometric forecasting, causal inference and GenAI systems such as RAG, assistants and agentic workflows, and own them through to production, embedded directly with the domain experts who will use them across global functions and our affiliates around the world.

Your Responsibilities Will Include


Translating commercial questions into data science and ML solutions that ship
Developing segmentation, targeting, propensity and causal inference models for commercial use cases, for example owning the predictive models behind new market launches and building the segmentation and look-alike models that tell sales representatives which HCPs and institutions to prioritise
Building GenAI applications end to end, including RAG pipelines, assistants, agentic solutions and workflow automation
Working with siloed, fragmented or entirely new data
Evaluating models using the right statistical, ML and business metrics, and explaining assumptions, uncertainty and trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders
Designing models with production readiness in mind
Scoping ambiguous commercial problems independently and helping set the standard for how the team approaches decision science and productionisation



You don’t need to be equally expert in classical data science and GenAI. We’re looking for real depth in one, genuine curiosity for the other and a willingness to build across both.

Your new team

You’ll join GCX’s newly established Data, Insights and AI team, responsible for establishing a new commercialisation intelligence layer and for building competitively differentiating predictive intelligence loops. We stay close to the business to make sure what we build gets used. The team is young enough that you’ll help shape its culture and ways of working. This is a build-from-scratch opportunity, not a seat on an established team.

Your Skills And Qualifications

We are looking for deep expertise in one or more of the following: statistics, econometrics, forecasting, causal inference, segmentation or applied/commercial ML; model production and MLOps; or GenAI engineering, including LLM applications, RAG and agents.

You will bring


Several years of experience building, deploying or supporting data science, ML, statistical or AI models using real commercial or business data
Strong Python and SQL skills, solid engineering practice including Git, documentation, tested and reusable code, and a strong grasp of model validation, interpretation and business impact
Experience with predictive models in a commercial or pharmaceutical setting
Clear communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and genuine interest in the commercial problem, not only the model
Comfort with AI-assisted development tooling such as Cursor or GitHub Copilot
An MSc, PhD or equivalent practical experience in statistics, econometrics, data science, mathematics, computer science, engineering or a related quantitative field



Depending on your strengths, you will also bring depth in several of


Practical MLOps, including CI/CD for models, model registries, experiment tracking and model monitoring
Hands-on GenAI, including LLM applications, embeddings, vector search, retrieval, evaluation, prompt engineering, agents and workflow solutions
APIs and backend development, testing and CI/CD
Experience taking analytical and AI solutions into production using modern MLOps and DataOps practices, including version control, automated testing, deployment and monitoring.



It is an advantage if you bring


A track record of taking classical models or AI applications into production, with strong understanding of reliability, monitoring, versioning, security, access control and maintainability
Experience with LLM evaluation, prompt and version management, guardrails and observability, and with monitoring quality, latency, reliability and cost
Experience from pharmaceuticals, healthcare, life sciences, commercial analytics or consumer behavior



Our promise to you

Lundbeck offers an inspiring workplace and innovative culture, where our curiosity, accountability and adaptability enable us to transform lives. We want to go faster and further on addressing the big unmet needs of people living with brain disorders. We offer rewarding careers with a mix of exciting tasks and development opportunities that are balanced with initiatives focused on your well-being.

We need every brain in the game, and at Lundbeck, we are committed to building a workforce that is as diverse as the people we serve. Read more about our commitment at www.lundbeck.com/global/about-us/our-commitment/diversity-and-inclusion.

Annual base salary range: 786 000 - 1 081 300 DKK gross

At Lundbeck, we are committed to fair and transparent pay. Please note that the final base salary within the stated range will be based on relevant qualifications, skills, competencies, and level of proficiency as well as internal pay equity.

Apply now

Upload your CV and include a few lines about your motivation for applying. We ask you not to include a photo or personal information that does not relate to your professional experience.

If you have questions, please contact Frederikke Bruhn Sørensen, Director Data, Insights and AI Solutions at feor@lundbeck.com.

Applications must be received by 16 October 2026.

Learn more about us at www.lundbeck.com, LinkedIn or Instagram (@h_lundbeck).

Title: Senior Data Scientist
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands.

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth.

We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.

Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow.

For more information, visit WPP.com.

Why we're hiring:

We are expanding our data science capability to develop a state-of-the-art system for estimating and understanding the size and characteristics of marketing and advertising audiences.

This role offers the opportunity to apply Bayesian statistics, advanced mathematical thinking and production-quality engineering to complex problems with meaningful industry impact.

What You’ll Be Doing


Develop and implement Bayesian statistical models and other advanced analytical methods to estimate audience sizes and characteristics.
Translate complex mathematical and statistical questions into robust, explainable data-driven solutions.
Build and maintain production-ready Python packages, including unit tests and clear technical documentation.
Collaborate with data scientists, engineers and other specialists to design, build and refine analytical solutions.
Work with diverse data formats and help maintain data quality and integrity throughout the analytics pipeline.
Use cloud computing resources to support scalable data processing and model deployment.
Contribute to Git repositories, code reviews and sound version-control practices while adapting to evolving priorities.


Who You’ll Be Working With

You’ll join a multidisciplinary team working on challenging statistical, mathematical and conceptual problems. The team values rigorous thinking, open discussion, knowledge sharing and practical solutions.

You’ll collaborate closely with colleagues who bring different technical perspectives and areas of expertise, contributing to an environment where ideas are tested constructively and improved together.

What You’ll Bring


Advanced knowledge of probability and statistics, including a strong foundation in Bayesian methods, gained through postgraduate study or equivalent professional experience.
Advanced Python programming skills, including package development, unit testing and working with multiple data formats.
Demonstrated ability to solve complex mathematical, statistical or conceptual problems.
Experience using Git, repositories and collaborative code-review practices.
Experience with a cloud computing platform such as AWS, GCP or Azure.
The ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and collaborate effectively with colleagues from different disciplines.
A thoughtful, structured approach to exploring unfamiliar problems and evaluating potential solutions.


Who you are:

You're open: We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic: We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary: we are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people – We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work.

Scale and opportunity – We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work – Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

WPP is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.

Who We Are

Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact.

To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures—and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive.

We Are BCG X

We’re a diverse team of more than 3,000 tech experts united by a drive to make a difference. Working across industries and disciplines, we combine our experience and expertise to tackle the biggest challenges faced by society today. We go beyond what was once thought possible, creating new and innovative solutions to the world’s most complex problems. Leveraging BCG’s global network and partnerships with leading organizations, BCG X provides a stable ecosystem for talent to build game-changing businesses, products, and services from the ground up, all while growing their career. Together, we strive to create solutions that will positively impact the lives of millions.

What You'll Do

Our BCG X teams own the full analytics value-chain end to end: framing new business challenges, designing innovative algorithms, implementing, and deploying scalable solutions, and enabling colleagues and clients to fully embrace AI. Our product offerings span from fully custom-builds to industry specific leading edge AI software solutions.

As a Data Scientist and Senior Data Scientist, you'll be part of our rapidly growing team. You'll have the chance to apply data science methods and analytics to real-world business situations across a variety of industries to drive significant business impact. You'll have the chance to partner with clients in a variety of BCG regions and industries, and on key topics like climate change, enabling them to design, build, and deploy new and innovative solutions.

Additional responsibilities will include developing and delivering thought leadership in scientific communities and papers as well as leading conferences on behalf of BCG X. Successful candidates are intellectually curious builders who are biased toward action, scrappy, and communicative.

We Are Looking For Talented Individuals With a Passion For Data Science, Statistics, Operations Research And Transforming Organizations Into AI Led Innovative Companies. Successful Candidates Possess The Following


Comfortable in a client-facing role with the ambition to lead teams
Likes to distill complex results or processes into simple, clear visualizations
Explain sophisticated data science concepts in an understandable manner
Love building things and are comfortable working with modern development tools and writing code collaboratively (bonus points if you have a software development or DevOps experience)
Significant experience applying advanced analytics to a variety of business situations and a proven ability to synthesize complex data
Deep understanding of modern machine learning techniques and their mathematical underpinnings, and can translate this into business implications for our clients
Have strong project management skills


What You'll Bring

Technologies

Programming Languages: Python

Title: Lead Data Scientist
Description:
Twoday is one of the leading digital transformation partners in Northern Europe with a global presence. With approximately 3,000 technologists, we collaborate with the most admired private and public organizations to deliver cutting-edge digital solutions. Our deep industry expertise includes Data & AI, software development, digital experiences, and business applications. Operating across the Nordics and Lithuania, our team serves over 8,000 customers and supporting their digital transformation journeys. 

We are looking for an experienced Lead Data Scientist to join our AI team!

Most organizations have no shortage of ideas for what to model. Far fewer can turn a vaguely stated business problem into a well-posed prediction task, pick the algorithmic approach that fits it, and defend the result when someone asks how the number was produced. That gap is where you come in. You will lead the analytical work that turns a customer's business problem into a model that holds up, and then into something they actually use, alongside data engineers, AI/ML engineers, cloud architects, and software developers on some of the largest Data & AI teams in the Nordics.

You will set the analytical direction on our most demanding engagements, and you will grow the people who deliver them.

What are we looking for?

You are a scientist and a builder. Given a business problem stated in a customer's own words, you can work out what should be predicted, at what granularity, against which target, with what horizon, and what a good result would even look like. You are rigorous about how you validate a result, and you have seen enough projects to have opinions about which problems are worth modelling at all and which should be solved another way.

We expect you to bring:


Several years of hands-on data science experience, including a number of models you have taken past the prototype stage and to production.
Proven strength in translating a business objective into a formal AI/ML problem: defining the target variable and unit of analysis, agreeing what success means with the people who will use the model, and saying early when the data will not support the question.
Deep predictive modelling craft: classification, regression, time series and generative AI, and the ability to set the modelling standard for others.
Judgement about algorithmic choice: when a well-specified baseline or classical statistical model is enough, when a heavier method earns its cost, and when the problem is not a prediction problem at all.
Solid applied statistics: honest validation, uncertainty, and the ability to explain what a result does and does not support.
Strong software fundamentals to write code others can build on.
Experience on Azure: Azure Machine Learning, Databricks, or Microsoft Fabric (Experience from AWS or GCP transfers, and we will not hold it against you.)
Experience applying generative AI where it genuinely fits, including RAG architectures and the evaluation of prompts and models.
An understanding of what governance means in practice: reproducibility, model documentation, GDPR, bias and fairness considerations, and the documentation the EU AI Act increasingly requires.
The ability to explain a technical trade-off to a customer's business stakeholder without flattening it into a slogan, and to push back when the question being asked is not the question that matters.
Leadership shown through analytical direction, mentoring, and raising the standard of the work around you.
Fluent spoken and written Danish is a requirement.


Will your responsibilities be?


Lead the analytical design of AI and ML solutions for our customers, from problem framing and feasibility through to a validated, documented model in production.
Run framing sessions with customers: shape the business problem into a prediction task with a defined target, a defined decision it supports, and success criteria the business recognises, and write down the assumptions the solution rests on.
Own the algorithmic approach: baselines, method selection and the reasoning behind it, validation strategy, and the honest assessment of what the model is worth.
Set analytical standards for the team: reproducibility, experiment tracking, documentation, and review of each other's work.
Work directly with customers: shape the approach, challenge requirements when they need challenging, and translate between business outcomes and what the data can support.
Mentor data scientists, and grow the data science capability across our Danish teams.
Take part in scoping and pre-sales for AI initiatives, where your judgement on feasibility and data readiness carries real weight.
Keep us current: evaluate new methods and tooling with a clear eye for what actually earns a place in customer delivery.
Engage as an local ambassador and expert in our global AI/ML offerings


About you


You take ownership and are comfortable working in complex environments
You are pragmatic and focus on delivering real-world value
You enjoy working across disciplines and bridging gaps within teams
You lift the people around you, colleagues and the customer's own specialists, and you leave a team more capable than you found it


What can we offer?

twoday is located in modern offices in 30 locations in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, and Lithuania. We have a strong and unique social environment with highly engaged employees. If you are the candidate we are looking for, you will have a central role with exciting opportunities to develop in an international and innovative group, with exciting products and services within technology and software. You will also have the flexibility to "jump" and work from one of our headquarters in Oslo, Stockholm, Copenhagen, Helsinki, or Vilnius at times.

Diversity & Inclusion

Are you not meeting all the requirements listed? Studies have shown that women and other minority groups are less likely to apply for a job if they don't meet every qualification. We're dedicated to build a workplace of diversity and inclusion. If you are excited about this role but your previous experience does not match the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Title: Junior Data Scientist

Level: Junior-Level Engineer, Data & Technology Solutions

Location: Copenhagen

Reporting to: Lead Engineer

About Open Intelligence:

We are the Activation arm of WPP Open Intelligence. Our team builds the foundational data infrastructure and high-performance edge services that power WPP’s position in the market. With approximately one-third of all global media spend flowing through WPP, our platform operates at the core of this massive network—deeply integrated and adopted by the largest supply-side partners in the AdTech industry. Operating at our scale presents unique engineering challenges. Our edge services currently handle over 60,000 classification requests per second, while our contextual classification pipelines process 10,000 requests per second. With operations spanning the US, UK, and ongoing expansion into EMEA and APAC, our infrastructure continuously interacts with up to 98% of the population in our active markets. We are an engineering-led team focused on building robust, scalable, and highly reliable systems.

Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for a Junior Data Scientist who is curious about turning data into clear, trustworthy insights. You care more about sound statistical thinking, clean analysis, and honest communication of limitations than about chasing any specific tool or model.

You are comfortable learning team standards for exploratory analysis, experimentation, and reproducible work, then delivering well-scoped analyses, metrics, and model-backed features under guidance from senior data scientists and engineers. You help define questions, validate assumptions, and document findings stakeholders can act on. You support building and evaluating models for defined problems, contribute to data quality and feature understanding, and investigate metric or model anomalies with mentorship. You bring strong hands-on skills in Python or R plus solid SQL, a solid grasp of core statistics and machine learning concepts, and familiarity with visualization and storytelling. Experience with notebooks or scripts, Git, and basic validation of analysis code matters; some exposure to a cloud or modern data stack — or strong motivation to learn in production — is enough to start. Openness to AI coding assistants to learn and work more effectively is welcome.

Beyond the technical craft, you communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences, ask questions when stuck, and share learnings in stand-ups. You take ownership of the quality of your analysis and are motivated by continuous learning, experimentation, and growing into production data science with the team.

WHY ARE WE HIRING We are at a critical inflection point in our growth and need to scale our engineering team to tackle an expanding set of complex challenges. As the digital ecosystem evolves, we are actively developing and releasing a new catalog of privacy-preserving data products. These solutions are designed to scale advanced targeting capabilities while remaining uncompromising on our promise to protect user privacy.

To support this product evolution, our infrastructure is undergoing massive global expansion. By the end of this year, we will be fully operational across the rest of the EMEA and APAC regions. Concurrently, we are deepening our integrations to support even more of the largest supply-side partners in the AdTech industry. We are hiring because we need strong engineering talent to help us architect for this next order of magnitude in scale—ensuring our systems remain resilient, performant, and compliant as our global footprint and feature set rapidly expand.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:


Learn and apply team standards for exploratory analysis, experimentation, and reproducible data science work.
Partner with product, analysts, and data engineers to deliver well-scoped analyses, metrics, and model-backed features under guidance from senior data scientists and engineers.
Help define questions, validate assumptions, and document findings so stakeholders can act on clear, trustworthy insights.
Support building and evaluating models or statistical approaches for defined problems, including basic monitoring and sanity checks after deployment.
Contribute to data quality checks, feature understanding, and lightweight governance so inputs and outputs stay reliable and interpretable.
Investigate anomalies in metrics or model behavior, document root causes, and implement fixes or escalations with mentorship.
Stay curious and proactive: ask questions, share learnings in stand-ups, and explore methods and tools that help the team move faster and smarter.


What You Will Need


Clear communication skills and the ability to explain analysis, limitations, and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
Up to ~2 years of experience in data science, analytics, applied statistics, or a related internship/graduate role.
Strong hands-on skills in Python or R for analysis, plus solid SQL for querying and transforming data.
Solid grasp of statistics and core machine learning concepts (e.g. regression, classification, evaluation metrics, train/test splits, overfitting).
Experience producing clear analysis in notebooks or scripts, with version control (Git) and basic testing or validation of analysis code.
Comfort working with structured (and ideally some unstructured) datasets; experience cleaning, joining, and aggregating data for analysis.
Familiarity with visualization and storytelling (e.g. Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, ggplot, or BI tools) to communicate results effectively.
Some exposure to a cloud or modern data stack (GCP, AWS, or Azure; warehouses, batch pipelines, or feature stores), or strong motivation to learn in production.
Enthusiasm for data, experimentation, and continuous learning.
Openness to using AI coding assistants and prompt engineering to learn faster and work more effectively.


NICE TO HAVE


Familiarity with AdTech- and/or MarTech data, metrics, and terminology.
Experience with experiment design, A/B testing, or causal thinking at a basic level.
Exposure to MLOps concepts (model packaging, batch scoring, simple monitoring) or collaboration with data engineering on pipelines.
Experience contributing in a monorepo or large shared codebase.
Awareness of data privacy basics and responsible handling of sensitive data.
Portfolio, Kaggle, coursework, or side projects demonstrating end-to-end analysis or modeling.


If you are ready to be at the forefront of the AdTech industry, shaping its future, and driving success for both our clients, we encourage you to apply and join our team.

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

WPP is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong

Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
About The Role

We are looking for an Enterprise AI & Data Science Analyst to join our Strategy & Consulting – Data & AI team. This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about artificial intelligence, data science, analytics, and transforming data into business value.

As part of our multidisciplinary AI team, you will work alongside data scientists, AI engineers, strategists, and industry experts to help clients solve complex business challenges using data and AI. You will support the development of analytical models, AI solutions, and insights that drive innovation and measurable outcomes across industries.

Title: Data Scientist
Description:
About Wash World

Wash World runs more than 200 automatic car wash halls in Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Germany, and washed over 4 million cars in 2025. Every hall has cameras, sensors and payment terminals, so a lot of operational data comes in every day. We want to use that data to find faults in the wash machines automatically.




Who you'll work with

You will work from our office in Copenhagen Ø, as part of the development team: three developers, two IT operations staff and one data analyst. Because the team is small, you will work directly with the people who run the systems you build on, and decisions get made quickly.

You will own your projects from your first week, including the choice of tools and models that suit the problem. As data and ML work at Wash World grows, you will have the opportunity to grow into the lead role for the area.




How we build

AI coding agents are at the centre of how we work. We use them every day to write, test and ship code across the stack, and you will do the same, from data pipelines and database migrations to model training and deployment. We expect you to know how to work with agents well. That means giving them the right context, splitting work into tasks they can handle, and reviewing and testing what they produce before it ships. The code is still yours, and you are responsible for it.




Your impact

As a Data Scientist at Wash World, you will use camera footage, customer feedback and operational data to detect faults in our wash machines. You will also build and run the systems that put this into production.

Your main project is computer vision on hall footage, detecting problems with brushes, dryers, foam, high pressure and car positioning. Part of the work is finding out which approach works. That may mean evaluating vision-language models, or curating a proper labelled dataset and training a dedicated classifier. Either way, good labels come first: you will combine customer complaints, customer service reviews and technician reports into training and evaluation datasets, and check that each label means what it appears to.




You will also work on the data underneath. That includes restructuring MySQL and PostgreSQL schemas, writing safe migrations, tuning queries and keeping production data in sync with BigQuery. You will deploy and operate your own work on Google Cloud, and help the rest of the development team where your skills fit.

Our current stack is Laravel (PHP) and Node.js/TypeScript for production services and Python for machine learning, with MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis and BigQuery, running on Google Cloud (Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud Storage and Cloud Build).




Your qualifications and skills

A bachelor's, master's or PhD in data science, computer science, machine learning or a related field. Recent graduates are welcome, and so are candidates with up to 4 years of experience. Bachelor's students may be considered if they have additional entrepreneurial experience or supporting details.
Hands-on experience building software with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, ideally on more than small scripts. You know how to set them up with project instructions and tools, when to trust their output, and how to check it.
Experience applying machine learning or computer vision to real-world data. A thesis or project counts.
Strong SQL and a solid understanding of relational database design, including keys, indexing, normalisation and migrations in PostgreSQL and/or MySQL
Programming experience in at least one of PHP (Laravel / Slim), Python or TypeScript (Node.js)
Experience with Docker and with deploying something to the cloud yourself, preferably on GCP. A personal or university project is fine.
Ability to own a problem from start to finish, and to say clearly when something cannot work, for example when a camera cannot see a fault
Good written and spoken English. Danish is not required, but knowledge of the language is an advantage.




Also valued: Kubernetes and Terraform, CI/CD, video tooling (ffmpeg, RTSP) and NVR/VMS systems, vision-language models and fine-tuning, self-hosted inference, Redis caching and pub/sub, BigQuery or dbt, and experience handling personal data under GDPR.




Hiring process

We will first conduct a virtual interview to determine whether there is a good fit. Then you will be invited to the office to conduct a follow-up interview and talk to the team if applicable.

Title: Quantitative analyst for the Quantitative Weather Analysis team
Description:
Quote

By combining multidimensional weather data, machine learning and market understanding, you’ll help shape trading decisions and optimise the balancing of our renewable asset portfolio.

Here’s what the job entails

In the role, you will work at the intersection of weather data modelling and fundamental forecasting, driving research and innovation within quantitative weather analysis.

More specifically, your responsibilities include:


conducting research in AI- and data-driven weather modelling within a power trading context
developing and improving fundamental forecasting solutions that translate weather signals into actionable power market insights
performing ad hoc weather and market analyses to support trading, renewable asset balancing and commercial decision-making
exploring new data sources, modelling approaches and analytical methods to strengthen our quantitative weather capabilities
turning research and analysis into robust, scalable solutions that can be used directly by traders and algorithms


Meet your team

You will join our Quantitative Weather Analysis team, where we develop weather-driven insights, forecasts and models that support trading decisions and renewable asset optimisation across our business.

We are a team of specialists with backgrounds in data science, physics and computational biophysics. We take our work seriously, but not ourselves, and aim to create an informal atmosphere and a team where people genuinely enjoy working together. We also value spending time with each other beyond the task at hand, whether that is grabbing a coffee, having lunch or simply catching up during the day. Together, we have built a culture where we help each other, share knowledge freely and feel comfortable asking questions or challenging ideas.

But enough about us… over to you!

As you will be working deeply with quantitative modelling and large datasets, we imagine that you take a curious and proactive approach to your tasks. You enjoy digging into how things work with a research-to-action mindset and challenge existing approaches when you see room for improvement. We also expect that you are comfortable taking ownership of projects while collaborating with stakeholders across the organisation.

Furthermore, we imagine that you:


have an educational background in Economics, Physics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Data Science or a related quantitative field
are experienced in writing production-quality, maintainable code in Python
are comfortable working in Linux-based environments and using common command-line tools
have a solid quantitative foundation and can work with statistical, mathematical or data-driven modelling
can work with large, complex datasets and transform data-driven insights into practical solutions
are curious about the power trading domain and has an execution and collaborative mindset


Please note that prior knowledge of the energy sector is not required for this role.

Title: Data Scientist, Q&A Analyst
Description:
About Us

Hoopoz is a SaaS platform that helps brands monitor digital advertising, identify potential compliance violations and turn scattered signals into evidence they can act on. By bringing monitoring and analysis into one place, we help teams understand what is happening across their markets and where action is needed.

Our team brings together experts from Lithuania, Denmark, Croatia and Ukraine. Together, we are building a clearer picture of how advertising connects to the businesses and affiliates behind it. We explain our findings clearly, support our conclusions with evidence and handle sensitive information with discretion.

Why this role?

You will own that question and measure how our detection actually performs, find where it breaks, and improve it. This role calls for someone who is not satisfied with an accuracy number, who asks what it was measured on and what happens at the edges. You should enjoy building methods where none exists yet, and taking responsibility for conclusions others will act on.

What we are looking for

3+ years of hands-on data science experience, with models or analyses you took from raw data to production
Strong Typescript, Python and SQL experience, and fluency with the standard data science stack (pandas, scikit-learn, or similar)
Solid grounding in evaluation — precision, recall and the trade-offs between them
Experience designing QA frameworks and tracking quality metrics 
Experience building and maintaining labelled datasets — sampling, annotation guidelines, agreement, class imbalance
You turn findings into recommendations people act on
Fluent in English

Considered a strong advantage

Experience with NLP or content classification: text detection, multilingual data, or working with LLMs and RAGs
Background in trust & safety, content moderation, fraud detection, AdTech or compliance-driven products
Experience designing evaluation frameworks from scratch
Familiarity with regulated industries (iGaming, fintech, insurance, pharma) and what evidence means there
Knowledge of the EU or USA regulatory landscape around online content and advertising (DSA, FTC, consumer protection, advertising standards)

What we offer

Ownership of a function
Direct line to founders
Fully remote position and flexibility

Title: Senior Associate - Data Science
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Senior Associate - Data Science

Consultant

Copenhagen · full time · permanent

This search is handled confidentially by Black Swans Exist. We name the company in the first conversation.




In short

You become the person the client calls. You own the relationship, you stand behind the delivery, and you build real depth in one field instead of being thrown between unrelated projects.

"Senior" here is about ownership, not years served. The sweet spot is two to five years of consulting experience.




About the company

We are recruiting for a Danish company in Copenhagen that builds and delivers software for the earliest stage of drug discovery.




When a pharmaceutical company develops a new drug, it has to decide which molecules are worth testing in the lab. The number of possibilities is effectively infinite. The lab can handle around a hundred.

This company builds the tools that find the right hundred — from choosing the target and the modality through to designing and screening the molecules.




The business model is a technology-driven consultancy. Their platform covers roughly 90% of the need out of the box, and the last 10% is built bespoke for each research project. That is why they deliver in a fraction of the time their competitors need.

They are around ten people, profitable, and the entire business has been built on referral. Their clients are pharma and biotech companies.




The role

The company has consultants who do the work at the client site, and a few more experienced people who own the client relationship itself. They need more of the second kind. That is you.

You own the client relationship — their single point of contact, and the person who holds the whole picture of what was promised and what is being delivered.
You deliver yourself. This is not a project management role. Clients will not accept someone who moves tickets around a board — you need to understand the problem and be part of solving it.
You are seen as a leader, not an engineer. That is the difference between being in the room and running the meeting.
You think on your feet. The client raises a problem mid-meeting and you can sketch a way forward while you are still sitting there.
You build depth. One field, one discipline, one kind of client — and you get genuinely good at it.




What you need

Two to five years in consulting — IT, technology, data or management. You have delivered at client sites and know how a client relationship feels when it is working and when it is not.
Technical level of a data scientist. You can code and follow the models. You do not need to be the strongest technologist in the building — that seat is taken.
A track record of moving. You have progressed faster than your peers, or done something else that was objectively hard and finished it.
Composure under pressure. The hard part of this job is the moment a client asks something you do not have an answer to. Going defensive is not an option.
People like being in a room with you. It is not on any CV, and it still decides how much business comes out of a relationship.




Nice to have - not required

Life science, pharma or biotech exposure. A pharma client on a past project counts. Fewer than half of the current team have a life science background.
Danish. A real advantage with Danish clients, but several of the team and several of the clients do not speak it. For the right person, language is not a blocker.
A computer science degree is not needed. Several of the strongest people on the team come from engineering or AI.




Why you would say yes

You become an expert in something. The most common reason good consultants leave the big firms is that they are moved between clients and never get truly good at anything. Here you pick one field and build hard, tangible skills around it.
The work matters. What you do ends up in medicines meant to help people.
You own the client from day one. No partner above you taking the meeting. Ten people, no layers, direct access to the people who decide.
There is somewhere to grow. The company would rather develop its commercial leaders from within. If that is the direction you want, the path exists.







If you are curious, write or call. No obligation, and we treat every approach confidentially.

Per Christensen · Managing Director & Co-Founder · Black Swans Exist

Title: Data Analyst / Biostatistician – Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS) Department of Clinical Immunology, Aarhus University Hospital
Description:
Data Analyst / Biostatistician – Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS) Department of Clinical Immunology, Aarhus University Hospital,

We are seeking a data analyst with strong statistical and data analytical skills to join the Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS). The ideal candidate enjoys working with large, complex datasets and is also interested in the biological and clinical questions behind the data.

What We Offer

DBDS is a national research project built on one of the world's largest biobanks, with more than 180,000 participants and over 3 million plasma samples. The study combines laboratory and registry data with phenotype data collected through, for example, questionnaires. Our research covers a wide range of topics, including how genetic factors and plasma biomarkers can predict disease. DBDS is a unique cohort because of its granular longitudinal data and blood samples, which allow us to study biomarker change over time.

The position offers an exceptional opportunity to work with large, complex datasets in a research environment where data analysis is closely integrated with clinical and biological research. You will be part of an interdisciplinary team and apply your analytical skills to research with the potential to improve public health.

The Department of Clinical Immunology (Blodbank og Immunologi) at Aarhus University Hospital is Central Denmark Region's specialist department for clinical immunology. The department has approximately 220 employees and is responsible for producing blood components; laboratory testing, diagnostic investigations and advisory services in transfusion medicine and transplant immunology; HIV and hepatitis testing; autoimmune diagnostics; and the investigation of immunodeficiencies.

Job Description

As a data analyst in DBDS, you will analyse large, complex longitudinal datasets based on registry, questionnaire and biomarker data. You will contribute to research projects across DBDS and help translate research questions into robust analyses and meaningful results.

You will plan and conduct statistical analyses and select methods suited to each research question. You will collaborate closely with researchers, data managers and statisticians within the department and across the national DBDS network, where you will advise researchers on statistical methods and help them plan and interpret their analyses.

You will also contribute to the day-to-day operation of DBDS, including occasional data management and data quality tasks as needed.

Your profile

Ideally, you have a background in statistics, biostatistics, bioinformatics, mathematics, data science or a related field. You have strong skills in advanced data analysis, in developing and applying AI and machine learning methods, or both. What matters most is a solid understanding of statistical principles and the ability to select, apply and critically assess the methods best suited to each research question and dataset. A PhD or equivalent experience is preferred.

It is important to us that you


have experience handling and analysing large longitudinal datasets
have strong skills in R, Python or similar for data analysis and processing
have a solid understanding of statistical methods and can select appropriate models for each research question
have experience with, or an interest in, registry data and/or biomarker data
can plan and carry out analyses independently
can interpret data and communicate results clearly and precisely
understand, or are keen to learn about, the biological and clinical questions behind the analyses
work in a structured way and can manage several tasks at once
collaborate effectively and thrive in interdisciplinary settings
have strong communication skills in English.


Experience with epidemiological or population-based studies, or with biobank data, is an advantage.

Employment details

The position is based at the Department of Clinical Immunology, Aarhus University Hospital, in the research group led by Clinical Chair Professor and Chief Physician Christian Erikstrup.

This is a three-year fixed-term position with the possibility of extension. The position is intended to be full-time. The start date is January 1st 2027 or by agreement.

Salary and terms of employment

Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the applicable collective agreement in Central Denmark Region. Employment is conditional upon a satisfactory child-related record check.

Application and contact

Applications may be written in Danish or English and must be received no later than November 8th 2026.

Interviews are expected to be held shortly thereafter. For further information about the position, please contact Clinical Chair Professor and Chief Physician Christian Erikstrup per mail christian.erikstrup@skejby.rm.dk.

The postion is primarly a full-time position.

Employees undergoing redeployment who apply for the position have priority in accordance with the applicable rules.

Under the EU Pay Transparency Directive, which took effect on June 7th 2026, Central Denmark Region is required to inform you of the starting salary, or the starting salary range, for a position before you are offered employment.

Central Denmark Region's salary catalogue for most staff groups and positions in the region is available here (in Danish): Gennemsigtighed forud for ansættelse – Medarbejder.rm.dk

Title: Data Scientist for Clinical Data and Research Infrastructure (TAP)
Description:
Aalborg University seeks a Data Scientist to help establish Digital Heart, a cardiovascular data and AI research infrastructure developed with Aalborg University Hospital and other hospital partners.



The position is a full-time technical and administrative staff position (TAP), planned for 3.5 years, with a possible extension, based at Aalborg University.



The position is available from 1 November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.



You will collect and organise clinical data—including echocardiography, cardiac MRI, CT, ECG and electronic patient records—within a secure Trusted Research Environment (TRE). Your work will provide the foundation for cardiovascular research and AI development.



Your responsibilities:



Working closely with clinicians, hospital IT teams, researchers and our data manager, you will:

Coordinate clinical data extraction and secure transfer from participating hospitals.
Develop and maintain workflows for importing, processing and linking imaging, biosignal and patient record data.
Establish structured research datasets, databases and metadata documentation.
Implement data quality checks and approved procedures for pseudonymisation and secure data handling.
Deploy existing analysis and AI tools and support researchers in using the platform.

Your qualifications:



You hold a relevant master’s degree in data science, computer science, biomedical engineering, health informatics or a related field, or have equivalent experience.



We are looking for:

Strong Python and SQL skills and experience developing reliable data pipelines.
Experience integrating complex datasets, preferably from clinical or hospital systems.
A systematic approach to data quality, documentation and sensitive data.
The ability to work independently and collaborate with clinical and technical colleagues.

Experience with DICOM/PACS, electronic patient records, secure research environments or container technologies is an advantage.



What we offer:



You will join an interdisciplinary cardiovascular research environment and have substantial influence on the development of Digital Heart’s data infrastructure.

Title: Quant Researcher
Description:
Would you like to manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets – and use your quantitative skills to make better commercial decisions?




Join our Physical Asset Management team and take responsibility for your own areas of the portfolio. You will work hands-on with market analysis, quantitative models, pricing and PnL while building the market knowledge needed to spot where we can do things better.




The team

You will join Physical Asset Management at Norlys Energy Trading in Aalborg. We manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets, combining portfolio management with market analysis and quantitative methods. The work involves close interaction with colleagues across trading, origination and asset management.




The role

As a Quant Researcher, you will operate and develop parts of our renewable portfolio across Europe. Over time, you will become the go-to person for your areas of responsibility: understanding what moves the market, how it affects the portfolio and where there is room to improve performance.




The role has a strong quantitative element. You will build models to understand portfolio effects, develop PnL dashboards and work on pricing methodologies and trading automation. You will also investigate new markets and products and help turn promising ideas into new business.




Key responsibilities

The role combines running the portfolio today with improving how we work tomorrow. You will work independently on some areas and together with colleagues and stakeholders in others.




Maintain and operate our renewable portfolios across the EU.
Run your own areas of responsibility with a focus on profitable performance.
Follow your markets closely and build specialist knowledge within your areas.
Build and maintain quantitative models to analyse and optimise portfolio effects.
Develop pricing methodologies and identify ways to improve portfolio performance.
Build and maintain dashboards that show PnL for your portfolios.
Help automate trading tools and processes.
Investigate new markets and products that could create new business opportunities.
Work closely with key stakeholders and take part in relevant conferences and excursions.




The people who thrive in this kind of role are the ones who stay curious when the answer isn’t obvious. You’ll have room to dig into problems, form your own view and act on what you learn. And when the market changes, you need to be comfortable changing your mind with it.

— Peter Lumbye Thomsen, Head of Intraday Analytics




What we are looking for

You are comfortable working with numbers, code and complex market information, but analysis is not an end in itself for you. You want to use it to make decisions, improve the way we work and move things forward when the market changes.




We expect you to have:

An advanced degree in a quantitative field such as physics, economics, data science or mathematics.
Strong programming skills in Python, R or a similar language.
Experience with data analysis and statistical modelling.
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
A can-do attitude and a sense of urgency when something needs to move.
An understanding of why agility and speed-to-market matter in a changing market.
The ability to work well with different stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
Experience within power trading or finance is an advantage, but not a requirement.




What we offer

The role gives you room to build specialist knowledge while working hands-on with renewable portfolios across European power markets.

Your own areas of responsibility within renewable portfolio management.
The chance to build specialist knowledge of European power markets.
A role that combines quantitative work with commercial decision-making.
Exposure to new markets, products and business opportunities.
Close collaboration with colleagues and stakeholders across the business.
Participation in relevant conferences and excursions.




Interested?

If the combination of power markets, quantitative analysis and portfolio responsibility sounds like a good match for you, we would like to hear from you.

Title: Quantitative Researcher - Algorithmic Trading
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Join Copenhagen Energy Trading as our next Quantitative Researcher - Algorithmic Trading (Short-term Power Markets)

Copenhagen Energy Trading (CET) shapes the future of the energy transition by combining deep market expertise with technical excellence in data, quantitative research and engineering to drive, automate and optimise our trading operations.




We’re a small, elite team based in central Copenhagen specializing in power trading and asset management across Europe and North America. Technology is core to how we operate, powered by exceptional talent and one of Europe’s most advanced automated and analytical trading environments for power markets. But we're not done. We want to push automation and advanced analytics even further, and to do that we need more exceptional people.




The Opportunity

That’s where you come in. We’re looking for an outstanding Quantitative Researcher with a proven track record of building real-time algorithmic trading strategies that operate with high reliability in regulated industries. You'll play a key role in developing strategies for the European short-term power markets.




This isn't a narrow coding or analyst role. You'll have an end-to-end mandate, from prototyping and data engineering to strategy implementation, backtesting and low-latency execution in our algorithmic trading framework. You'll own your projects from idea to P&L, working autonomously alongside a close-knit group of software engineers, quantitative researchers and expert traders.




So, if you feel energized by the intersection of markets, advanced analytics and trading technology and you want to help build something that moves power to where it’s needed the most, then we must talk.




Responsibilities

Research and model the markets: Analyse energy market dynamics and turn your insights into predictive models that drive profitable trading strategies.
Own the data: Build and maintain high-quality datasets that combine fundamental and real-time market data.
Take strategies to production and keep them running: Own the path from research to live trading, shaping the systems, forecasting tools and data pipelines that run our strategies in real time. Once they're live, you'll monitor their performance, handle issues as they come up and make sure they trade reliably day to day.
Shape the team's direction: Work closely with engineers, quantitative researchers and traders to challenge ideas, share expertise and influence where we take our algorithmic trading next.
Master the domain: Become a domain expert and understand algorithmic trading architectures and order execution logic in the short-term power markets.




Who are you?

You have:

Quantitative expertise: A track record of building accurate forecasting models and trading strategies for financial or energy markets, with a rigorous approach to research and validation.
Software and data skills: Advanced Python skills, and the ability to write clean, efficient, reliable code, backed by solid computer science fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, system design). Strong data skills, from sourcing and cleaning to structuring complex datasets. Some experience with C++ would be a plus.
Ownership: The ability to work independently and deliver in a fast-paced environment.
Strong communication: Excellent problem-solving and communication skills with full professional proficiency in English.
Domain knowledge: A genuine interest in learning about power markets and systems. If you already have that domain knowledge, then that is a big plus.
Education: An advanced degree in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science or Engineering.




What We Offer

Growth environment: Be part of a young, ambitious, and expanding tech-driven trading company where talented people are given responsibility and room to grow.
Exceptional team: Work closely with experienced quantitative researchers, software engineers and power traders.
Competitive compensation and flexibility: Receive a competitive salary package with benefits and enjoy flexible work arrangements that support your work-life balance.
Strong culture: Participate in both social and professional events, including team sports, company parties, teambuilding and informal gatherings that strengthen our team spirit.
Central Copenhagen location: Work from our office in Carlsberg Byen, located in beautifully renovated historic Carlsberg buildings.




About Copenhagen Energy Trading

Copenhagen Energy Trading A/S was founded in 2021 and is part of Copenhagen Energy Group.




We specialize in short-term power trading across Europe and North America. Through technology, data, and market expertise, we develop discretionary and algorithmic trading strategies that help move power to where it is needed most.




Based in Copenhagen, we are building a collaborative, high-performance environment where talented people are trusted with responsibility and given the freedom to make an impact.




How to apply

If this opportunity feels like the right fit for you, we would love to hear from you.




Please apply via LinkedIn and submit your cover letter, CV, and university transcripts as a single PDF. Please note that applications that do not meet these requirements may not be considered.




Application deadline: October 23, 2026




If you have any questions, please contact Jens Christian Johannsen at jc@copenhagen-energy.com or Anna Schumann at as@copenhagen-energy.com.
