Title: Vil du hjælpe os med at udvikle FREMTIDENS KVÆGAVL?
Description:
Brænder du for data og statistik, og synes du koen er et fantastisk dyr? Vil du være med til at udvikle et mere bæredygtigt kvægbrug i Danmark? Så er du måske den kollega, vi leder efter til et spændende job i SEGES Innovation.




I SEGES Innovation tilbyder vi dig en karriere med mening. Vores innovation og viden gør en forskel både i hverdagen og på den lange bane. Vores specialister arbejder med alt fra klima og miljø, planter, dyr og digitale løsninger til vækst og vidensformidling. Sammen bidrager vi til de løsninger, der gør landbruget og fødevareproduktionen endnu mere bæredygtig.




I afdelingen for Husdyr søger vi lige nu en person med en uddannelse inden for agrobiologi, statistik, matematik, data science eller lignende. Din uddannelsesbaggrund er dog ikke det vigtigste. Det vigtigste er, at du har stærke analytiske evner, interesse for data og lyst til at være med til at udvikle grundlaget for avlsarbejdet med kvæg i Danmark og Norden.




Hvad skal du lave?

Som vores nye kollega bliver du en del af den afdeling, der har ansvar for udvikling og drift af avlsværdivurdering for malkekvæg, kødkvæg, får og geder. Vi er ni personer, der arbejder tæt sammen om alt fra indsamling af data på den enkelte ko til implementering af avancerede statistiske modeller. Du får ansvar for konkrete opgaver og projekter, men vi bruger aktivt hinandens viden og kompetencer. Vi har nemlig som regel travlt, og vores erfaring er, at vi når længst gennem samarbejde.




Dit arbejdsområde vil primært være udviklingsprojekter, hvor vi udvikler de avlsværdital, som landmænd og avlsorganisationer bruger til at vælge de bedste avlsdyr som forældre til næste generation. Det kan for eksempel være avlsværdital for reduceret metanudledning eller egenskaber, der forbedrer dyrevelfærd og sygdomsresistens. Grundlaget er store mængder data fra blandt andet genomiske tests og målinger på køer og kalve.




Noget af det, vi selv synes er allerbedst ved vores arbejde, er muligheden for at være med til at forme fremtidens projekter og faglige fokusområder. Derfor er opsamling, udvikling og prioritering af nye idéer en vigtig del af vores hverdag. Samtidig motiverer det os at se, at det vi udvikler, bliver anvendt i praksis hos landmændene og gør en reel forskel.




En typisk hverdag

Vi er praktiske talnørder, og vores projekter har typisk en varighed på 1 til 4 år. En normal arbejdsdag starter ofte med statistiske analyser eller udviklingsopgaver. Vi arbejder tæt sammen som gruppe og har faste morgenmøder tre gange om ugen, hvor vi kort deler status på vores opgaver og eventuelle udfordringer.




Selvom du har dine egne ansvarsområder, er der altid en erfaren kollega at sparre med, og Teams bliver flittigt brugt til både store og små spørgsmål i løbet af dagen. Efterhånden som du opbygger erfaring, vil du også få dialog med avlsrådgivere og landmænd samt mulighed for at præsentere resultater og anbefalinger.




Du får dermed en varieret hverdag med mulighed for både fordybelse, faglig udvikling og samarbejde.




Projektporteføljen for 2026 og 2027 er allerede fastlagt, men vi har gode muligheder for at tilpasse dele af opgaverne efter dine interesser og kompetencer.




Vi drømmer om, at du

Har lyst til at analysere store datasæt.
Har lyst til at udvikle nye idéer og eventuelt lede udviklingsprojekter.
Kan kommunikere klart og præcist, både mundtligt og skriftligt.
Kan programmere i SAS eller Python eller har lyst til at lære det.
Har interesse for dataanalyse og lyst til at lære mere om kvægproduktion og avl.




Det får du hos os

Du bliver en del af et stærkt fagligt miljø med mulighed for at udvikle dig inden for statistiske modeller, programmering, projektledelse og formidling af komplekse analyser.




Når du starter, har vi en plan klar for både din introduktion til gruppens arbejde og dine første opgaver på kort og længere sigt. Du får tilknyttet en kollega, som sikrer, at du kommer godt i gang.




Har du ikke et indgående kendskab til kvæg, er det ikke noget problem. Vi hjælper dig med at opbygge den nødvendige forståelse, og hvis du har lyst, sender vi dig gerne på besøg i en besætning, så du får et godt indblik i branchen og de problemstillinger, vi arbejder med.




Praktiske oplysninger

Ansættelse ønskes snarest muligt. Vi afholder samtaler løbende og ansætter, når vi har fundet den rette kandidat. Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte afdelingsleder Anders Fogh på telefon 51 73 73 23.




Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig og til at byde en ny kollega velkommen i arbejdet med at udvikle fremtidens bæredygtige kvægbrug.










Ved rekruttering hos SEGES Innovation prioriterer vi primært din faglige ekspertise og personlighed. Vi ser mangfoldighed som en styrke, derfor opfordres alle med de rette kompetencer til at søge - uanset etnisk tilhørsforhold, religion, kønsidentitet og alder.




SEGES Innovation er en uafhængig forsknings- og innovationsvirksomhed, der arbejder for en bæredygtig og konkurrencedygtig landbrugs- og fødevareproduktion. Vi kobler faglige indsigter med digitale teknologier, så ny viden kommer ud at virke i stalden, på marken og i hele værdikæden fra jord til bord.




Vores mange forskellige eksperter udgør et unikt fagmiljø i international topklasse med ca. 500 dedikerede kolleger, der arbejder ud fra værdierne Mod, Hjerte og Dybde og i tæt samspil med Danmarks mere end 30.000 landbrug, universiteter og uddannelsesinstitutioner, landbrugsrådgivere, fødevareproducenter, energiselskaber og myndigheder.

Sammen bidrager vi til de løsninger, der gør landbruget og fødevareproduktionen endnu mere bæredygtig.


I afdelingen for Husdyr søger vi lige nu en person med en uddannelse inden for agrobiologi, statistik, matematik, data science eller lignende. Din uddannelsesbaggrund er dog ikke det vigtigste. Det vigtigste er, at du har stærke analytiske evner, interesse for data og lyst til at være med til at udvikle grundlaget for avlsarbejdet med kvæg i Danmark og Norden.


Hvad skal du lave?

Som vores nye kollega bliver du en del af den afdeling, der har ansvar for udvikling og drift af avlsværdivurdering for malkekvæg, kødkvæg, får og geder. Vi er ni personer, der arbejder tæt sammen om alt fra indsamling af data på den enkelte ko til implementering af avancerede statistiske modeller. Du får ansvar for konkrete opgaver og projekter, men vi bruger aktivt hinandens viden og kompetencer. Vi har nemlig som regel travlt, og vores erfaring er, at vi når længst gennem samarbejde.


Dit arbejdsområde vil primært være udviklingsprojekter, hvor vi udvikler de avlsværdital, som landmænd og avlsorganisationer bruger til at vælge de bedste avlsdyr som forældre til næste generation. Det kan for eksempel være avlsværdital for reduceret metanudledning eller egenskaber, der forbedrer dyrevelfærd og sygdomsresistens. Grundlaget er store mængder data fra blandt andet genomiske tests og målinger på køer og kalve.


Noget af det, vi selv synes er allerbedst ved vores arbejde, er muligheden for at være med til at forme fremtidens projekter og faglige fokusområder. Derfor er opsamling, udvikling og prioritering af nye idéer en vigtig del af vores hverdag. Samtidig motiverer det os at se, at det vi udvikler, bliver anvendt i praksis hos landmændene og gør en reel forskel.


En typisk hverdag

Vi er praktiske talnørder, og vores projekter har typisk en varighed på 1 til 4 år. En normal arbejdsdag starter ofte med statistiske analyser eller udviklingsopgaver. Vi arbejder tæt sammen som gruppe og har faste morgenmøder tre gange om ugen, hvor vi kort deler status på vores opgaver og eventuelle udfordringer.


Selvom du har dine egne ansvarsområder, er der altid en erfaren kollega at sparre med, og Teams bliver flittigt brugt til både store og små spørgsmål i løbet af dagen. Efterhånden som du opbygger erfaring, vil du også få dialog med avlsrådgivere og landmænd samt mulighed for at præsentere resultater og anbefalinger.


Du får dermed en varieret hverdag med mulighed for både fordybelse, faglig udvikling og samarbejde.


Projektporteføljen for 2026 og 2027 er allerede fastlagt, men vi har gode muligheder for at tilpasse dele af opgaverne efter dine interesser og kompetencer.


Vi drømmer om, at du

  • Har lyst til at analysere store datasæt.
  • Har lyst til at udvikle nye idéer og eventuelt lede udviklingsprojekter.
  • Kan kommunikere klart og præcist, både mundtligt og skriftligt.
  • Kan programmere i SAS eller Python eller har lyst til at lære det.
  • Har interesse for dataanalyse og lyst til at lære mere om kvægproduktion og avl.


Det får du hos os

Du bliver en del af et stærkt fagligt miljø med mulighed for at udvikle dig inden for statistiske modeller, programmering, projektledelse og formidling af komplekse analyser.


Når du starter, har vi en plan klar for både din introduktion til gruppens arbejde og dine første opgaver på kort og længere sigt. Du får tilknyttet en kollega, som sikrer, at du kommer godt i gang.


Har du ikke et indgående kendskab til kvæg, er det ikke noget problem. Vi hjælper dig med at opbygge den nødvendige forståelse, og hvis du har lyst, sender vi dig gerne på besøg i en besætning, så du får et godt indblik i branchen og de problemstillinger, vi arbejder med.


Praktiske oplysninger

Ansættelse ønskes snarest muligt. Vi afholder samtaler løbende og ansætter, når vi har fundet den rette kandidat. Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte afdelingsleder Anders Fogh på telefon 51 73 73 23.


Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig og til at byde en ny kollega velkommen i arbejdet med at udvikle fremtidens bæredygtige kvægbrug.




Ved rekruttering hos SEGES Innovation prioriterer vi primært din faglige ekspertise og personlighed. Vi ser mangfoldighed som en styrke, derfor opfordres alle med de rette kompetencer til at søge - uanset etnisk tilhørsforhold, religion, kønsidentitet og alder.


SEGES Innovation er en uafhængig forsknings- og innovationsvirksomhed, der arbejder for en bæredygtig og konkurrencedygtig landbrugs- og fødevareproduktion. Vi kobler faglige indsigter med digitale teknologier, så ny viden kommer ud at virke i stalden, på marken og i hele værdikæden fra jord til bord.


Vores mange forskellige eksperter udgør et unikt fagmiljø i international topklasse med ca. 500 dedikerede kolleger, der arbejder ud fra værdierne Mod, Hjerte og Dybde og i tæt samspil med Danmarks mere end 30.000 landbrug, universiteter og uddannelsesinstitutioner, landbrugsrådgivere, fødevareproducenter, energiselskaber og myndigheder.

Title: Postdoc in Multi-Modal Behavioural Modelling - DTU Compute
Place: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Job Description

If you are looking to establish yourself as a researcher in the cross-disciplinary fields of machine learning and mental health, this postdoc position is for you.

At DTU Compute you will focus is on building multi modal models for mental health applications in a Danish context. You will collaborate with a mental health department at the hospital (Region H), startup companies, as well as Denmark’s AI research and development house, Alexandra Instituttet. Our joint grand solution project is providing foundational models (wearables, speech, video) for behavioural modelling across several mental health applications.

Responsibilities And Qualifications

As part of the position, you will be responsible for:


Data collection activities
Data annotation activities
Developing novel models for multi modalities, herein wearables, speech, and/or video
Pursuing the aims of making foundation models more representative.
Modelling data from mental health applications in collaboration with mental health experts
Conducting computational research experiments and disseminating these in research papers
Good collaborations with project partners (incl. hospitals and companies)


We are looking for you with


Outstanding interdisciplinary collaboration skills
Good organizational/project management skills
Excellent research skills in machine learning and an
Interest in mental health applications


As a formal qualification, you must hold a PhD degree (or equivalent).

We offer

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and terms of employment

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures .

The period of employment is 22 months. Start date is according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here .

Further information

Further information may be obtained from Line Clemmensen, Lkhc@dtu.dk .

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark .

Application procedure

Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 12 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:


Application (cover letter)
CV
Academic Diplomas (MSc/PhD – in English)
List of publications


Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk .

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Description:
Job Description

Are you interested in applying your data, engineering, cloud, or AI expertise within the Life Sciences industry? We are always looking for talented professionals to join the project teams driving this work forward.

At ADC, our Engineering & Analytics (Life Sciences) team is engaged across the full R&D data value chain for pharmaceutical and biotech organisations, from early discovery through clinical development. Our work spans scientific data engineering and GenAI solutions across omics, molecular data and AI engineering. We're also delivering data products and GenAI capabilities that support clinical development and operations within regulated LS environments.

Our team is actively working across the following areas within Life Sciences:


Omics engineering: building scientific data engineering and GenAI solutions across omics, molecular data and AI engineering, including data-analysis platforms.
Bioinformatics: delivering end-to-end AI solutions built on industry best practices, combining deep domain knowledge with engineering excellence for clinical and biological data.

LLM and generative AI applications in pharma: having hands-on experience building agentic and LLM-based products in regulated environments such as Databricks and Azure OpenAI.
Data engineering: building and maintaining pipelines and migration engineering that regulated enterprise rollouts depend on.


We welcome applications from all seniority levels, from junior professionals to experienced specialists and senior consultants.

Our teams are currently working on a wide range of projects, including:


Clinical, biomedical, omics, or pharmaceutical data
Reliable and scalable data pipelines
Cloud and data platforms such as Databricks
Technologies such as Python, SQL, Spark, and MLflow
Machine learning, LLMs, or generative AI within Life Sciences
Bioinformatics or computational biology solutions

Title: Quantitative Analyst
Description:
Do you want to gain a deep understanding of the power market and contribute directly to trading decisions? Do you thrive in a high‑paced, data‑driven environment where your analytical skills shape tomorrow’s strategies? If you’re ready for a role with real responsibility and impact, join our team as a Quantitative Analyst and help drive disciplined, high‑quality trading outcomes.




We are seeking a highly motivated individual with strong quantitative skills to join our team as a Quantitative Analyst. In this role, you will work closely with the team, applying data‑driven insights, modelling, and risk thinking to take ownership of disciplined trading decisions. Your ability to transform analysis and code into actionable insights will directly contribute to improving the quality and profitability of our trading decisions.




In this role, you will gain deep insights into our trading strategies and tools that provide a significant competitive advantage. You can expect a steep learning curve and growth opportunities in an environment where flat hierarchy and team spirit drive our success. You will experience a high degree of autonomy and see your own ideas come to life and see your ideas quickly evolve into tangible solutions that make a meaningful impact on our trading operations.




Key Responsibilities

Market Analysis: Conduct in-depth, data‑driven analysis of power markets including supply and demand fundamentals, regulatory developments, weather‑driven patterns, and geopolitical impacts to uncover actionable trading opportunities and support strategic decision‑making.
Risk Management: Implement robust risk management practices by monitoring position limits, conducting stress testing, and assessing exposure to volatile market conditions to ensure controlled and compliant trading activities.
Tool Development: Develop, maintain, and optimize a range of analytical, real‑time monitoring, and reporting tools that enhance trading decision‑making and operational efficiency. Build automated dashboards and data pipelines to produce accurate, timely reports on trading performance, risk metrics, and key market trends.
Model Development: Continuously improve trading models through back testing and market‑driven data analysis to strengthen and support profitable trading decisions.
Collaboration: Work closely with the team to enhance trading strategies and technical setup, ensuring clear and consistent communication across all team members.
Trading Application: Apply insights from analysis, modelling and risk assessment to confidently support and execute well‑founded trading decisions that meet all required risk, compliance, and performance standards.




Qualifications and Requirements

As a candidate, we expect you:

Hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree in mathematics‑economics, economics, statistics, engineering, or another quantitative field.
Have strong quantitative and analytical skills to interpret complex data and translate it into well‑founded trading insights.
Are proficient in Python and comfortable with coding. Experience with other code languages is considered an advantage.
Have a strong interest in financial and energy markets and a desire to deepen your understanding of power‑market dynamics.
Demonstrate excellent problem‑solving skills, high attention to detail, and the ability to adapt quickly to changing market conditions.
Communicate clearly and effectively, presenting technical and analytical concepts in a way that is easy for both technical and non‑technical team members to understand.




What We Offer

As an employer, we offer:

A full-time position that gives you the opportunity to apply your acquired skills.
Support in your role from experienced professionals.
Access to unique technologies and resources.
An opportunity to work at the forefront of power trading, contributing to groundbreaking strategies.
Opportunities for career growth and advancement.
Competitive compensation package.
A modern and brand-new office in the heart of Aarhus.
Professional and committed colleagues with high ambitions.
Inspiring, collaborative, and innovative work environment.
A place where your contributions are recognized and have a meaningful impact on the company's success.




A Profitable Growth Company with a Clear Vision

ENZEE is an ambitious growth company specialized in energy trading across the European continent. We envision a sustainable world and therefore, every day at ENZEE is a day with purpose. We believe that well-functioning and efficient energy markets are a necessity towards a net zero future which is exactly where we contribute with our expertise.




The ENZEE team consists of highly qualified, experienced, and knowledgeable industry professionals with a wide range of expertise in the energy markets. As a member of our team, you can expect a steep learning curve, great career growth opportunities, and the possibility of making a significant contribution.




Jobstart & Type

Full-time position
Location: Aarhus
As soon as possible




Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis, and we encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.




ENZEE is dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and therefore we encourage all candidates to apply, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disabilities.




If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact us at recruitment@enzeecommodities.com.

Title: Postdoctoral Position in AI Assistants for Clinical Decision Support
Description:
At the Center for Clinical Data Science (CLINDA), Department of Clinical Medicine, Aalborg University, we are looking for a full time postdoctoral researcher to join us in developing AI-based systems for clinical decision support in hospitals, starting December 1, 2026, or soon hereafter.  



The duration of the position is two years, with the possibility of extension.



Subject



Clinical decision support systems can assist healthcare professionals in diagnosing and monitoring health conditions by integrating information from multiple sources, including clinical notes, laboratory and pathology results, imaging (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI, and PET), clinical guidelines, and coding resources. Such systems can support clinical decision-making by helping clinicians synthesize heterogeneous clinical information and knowledge. 



Your work tasks



The aim of the position is to explore and develop AI agent technologies that can assist healthcare experts in daily clinical problem solving, especially in deciding on the most appropriate next steps in the diagnostic pathway. A central task will be to develop an interactive framework based on large language models (LLMs) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques, capable of synthesizing information from the diverse data types, and further help interpret the findings in the context of individual patients’ profile and history. Important research questions include how to design the agent framework; how to represent, retrieve, and utilize information from the different data modalities to ground the system’s reasoning in clinical evidence; how to best incorporate human-in-the-loop (HITL) functionality so users can interact with the agent’s reasoning process; and how to enable forecasting and simulations over multiple time steps.



The project will be conducted in close collaboration with clinical partners, providing access to data-rich healthcare environments and established diagnostic workflows. One key partner is the Diagnostic Center (DC) in Farsø, Denmark. This setting offers a unique opportunity to develop and evaluate AI-based clinical decision support systems using real-world patient data from individuals undergoing diagnostic evaluation for serious conditions, including cancer and other complex diseases.

Job Description

The Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) opens a 4 year full time position for an experienced scientist to work with satellite and in-situ observations to assess the suitability of hybrid-ML/AI and end-to-end data-driven methods to replace classical (physics based) methods in the production of future reanalyses (e.g. ERA7)

Most of the work is carried out in the Horizon Europe project, CHERRI, led by European Center for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). DMI has a task in the project to lead the activities about evaluating atmospheric reanalysis systems with a particular focus on oceans and the high latitudes, including ice sheets and sea ice. It is expected that you will be the technical and scientific lead on these activities that include developing a system which enables easy assessment of various NWP reanalysis products and on interpreting on the results to provide feedback to the model developers in CHERRI. DMI is a leading European developer and producer of remote sensing products, including surface temperature products for the global ocean and high latitudes, sea ice concentration and emissivity products for the Polar Oceans and you will use these products in the assessment.

In addition, you will participate in the work within the Copernicus Marine Service and the Copernicus Climate Change projects to produce operational and timely updates of the satellite surface temperature products.

You will work in close collaboration with dedicated and highly qualified colleagues in the remote sensing group and colleagues from other institutions across Europe and you will be writing peer reviewed publications and representing DMI in new research projects and in international organizations.

Main working tasks


Lead the tehnical and scientific development within the HEU CHERRI WP 9 “Work on NWP reanalysis model evaluation and diagnostics”
Develop diagnostics to assess the ability of hybrid-ML and end-to-end data-driven analysis methods to produce physically consistent earth-system states and trends.
Lead the communication and reporting to the project on the evaluation and diagnostics.
Develop and implement a processing code base that will enable multi model validation and intercomparison with satellite products, with focus on oceans and high latitudes.
Contribute to Copernicus Marine and C3S data processing
Represent DMI within the international science community through participation in international collaborations and contribute to new satellite missions.


Your Qualifications


Recognized scientist with expertise on NWP/Reanalysis evaluation.
Experience working with satellite observations.
Experience with physical ocean and sea ice processes.
Good communication skills and a scientific publication list.
Advanced programming skills in e.g. Python (preferrable) orFortran .
Experience with Linux and GIT
Good skills in oral and written English.
Can work well in a team in close collaboration with your colleagues.


The position is in the Danish National Centre for Climate Research (NCKF) at DMI, which employs approximately 80 scientists of which 20 are located in the Satellites and Arctic unit. We have a strong international profile which is also reflected in the many nationalities here and in an English "working language".

Employment and Salary

Will be according to the Danish Law and Agreements, specifically the Collective Agreement for State-Employed Academics (AC-overenskomsten). It will be possible to negotiate an addition to the basic salary depending on your qualifications and experience. DMI offers a flexible working week of 37 hours including a paid lunch break, and six weeks of paid vacation annually. If you come from abroad, there is a possibility for a reduced tax scheme the first 7 years.

For further details about the position, contact the head of the unit NCKF-Satellite and the Arctic: Jacob L. Høyer (telephone: +45 29 31 87 95 or by e-mail: jlh@dmi.dk).

At DMI, diversity is an important value for us, because we believe that an inclusive and versatile work environment strengthens task fulfilment. We work actively with diversity in our employee composition, which is reflected in our inclusive workplace with a balance between work life and family life. We encourage everyone to apply for the position regardless of age, gender, sexuality, religion or ethnicity.

Title: Data AI Engineer (AI & Analytics)
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Building trusted AI-powered analytics for healthcare training outcomes




Make an impact with Laerdal!

Laerdal Medical is a world leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training that uses immersive technologies and data-centric insights to increase survival and improve healthcare quality. Laerdal Copenhagen is our Center of excellence for Digital Learning, and on a global scale, we work with leading life-saving institutions around the world including emergency services, hospitals, ambulance services, first aid organizations, and educational institutions. Our products help these organizations save lives every day. We are a dynamic and energetic organization consisting of people from a wide variety of cultures and backgrounds. Our goal is to help save one million more lives, every year, by 2030, and to do so sustainably.




Position overview

We work in the space of advanced analytics for learners in healthcare and are looking to expand our team. In our area of Resuscitation Quality Improvement (RQI) we serve as the interface for varying roles in the healthcare system that want to know how their learners are doing, where they can improve and how prioritizing a high-quality training curriculum elevates the skills of their workforce.




Our product team spans multiple roles, backgrounds and nationalities and for the next major phase in how we deliver insights to users, we want your help:

Do you understand how to translate a vast structured data foundation into actionable insights for different user groups and metrics?

Do you have experience in advanced analytics, i.e. leveraging LLMs, statistics and ML? Have you implemented agentic systems? Do you know how to move from product idea to trustworthy user-facing feature in this space?

Do you want to help us on our mission to help save (even more) lives?




If you answered YES to those questions, don’t hesitate to apply with a brief personal motivation and CV and we might soon be getting to know each other in person!




What we want to build with you:

AI-Ready data foundation: guaranteeing high data quality for AI, refining the data model and ensuring efficient retrieval/search across our domain
Agentic data analyst: empower our analytics users to uncover individualized insights by combining traditional analytics with agentic workloads.
Operational excellence for AI: continuously learning and adapting the system while collaborating closely with product and design experts on the team




How you will contribute to the team:

Design and implement agentic product features for our custom advanced analytics platform
Understand and improve our domain data model
Partner with the Product Manager and Design Researcher to understand user needs, gather requirements and translate them into technical solutions
Ensure security/compliance and governed access for customers and internal users as well as safe guardrails for AI




Which skills you should bring (AI & data):

Hands-on experience in data modeling, production ready LLM solutions and using tools such as Langchain, Mastra, Embabel or other ADKs
Proficiency in using cloud data platforms and corresponding tools; e.g. PySpark, SQL, Databricks as well as the tools that enable search indexes, RAG or other integration patterns
Proven understanding of different agent workflow patterns and their benefits
(optional) Experience in data governance, semantic models and metadata management




Software engineering & other skills:

Knowledge of engineering practices and willingness to discuss them with peers; e.g. branching strategies, TDD, agile & DevOps principles
Advanced abilities in AI coding: harness engineering, skills development, context engineering, etc.
(optional) Knowledge in IaC tools and cloud solution architecture
(optional) Domain knowledge in healthcare and/or learning systems




Why join Laerdal Copenhagen?

Join a mission-driven team where your work helps improve healthcare and save lives around the world. You'll enjoy a high-trust, low-bureaucracy environment that values autonomy, collaboration, craftsmanship, and continuous learning. Our Copenhagen office, located in a historic warehouse in the city center, combines an ambitious, international culture with a relaxed atmosphere, great colleagues, and flexible working conditions. We are currently counting 160 colleagues in Copenhagen – a mix of talents across engineering, design, learning- and medical specialists, working in cross functional teams. As part of Laerdal Medical, you'll work locally with a talented team while being connected to a global organization of 2,200+ people dedicated to helping save one million more lives, every year, by 2030.




Learn more about our mission: One Million More Lives

Or get a glimpse of our office culture: Laerdal Copenhagen 2022 | Videos & Movies on Vimeo




Interested?

Apply with your CV and a short motivation explaining why this role speaks to you. (Remember, LinkedIn allows only one document, so please merge your CV and motivation letter into one file.)




If you have any questions that might keep you from applying, reach out by e-mail to Engineering Manager Jasper Hahn Jasper.Hahn@laerdal.com.




We are currently reviewing applications and about to set up first interviews. We will stop considering new applications by mid October.

You’ll work closely with analysts, traders, and platform teams to ensure high-quality data-driven insights. developing our new gas supply and demand to enable our gas trading and portfolio management activities
developing and improving gas and power market models for supply-demand and price formation.
integrating key drivers such as weather, fuel prices, outages, and interconnector flows into models.
ensuring model outputs reflect market behaviour across short- and mid-term horizons.

have a background in quantitative development, engineering, economics, or similar, or equivalent experience.
possess deep knowledge of European gas markets
write scalable, well-tested Python code and apply modern development practices.
are familiar with version control, CI/CD, and collaborative software development.
work confidently with data, including time series analysis, SQL, and data visualisation tools.
are motivated to build expertise in energy markets and translate it into models.
communicate clearly and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

Title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Arctic Sea-Ice and Initialised Climate Prediction
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
The Arctic is warming faster than any other region on Earth. DMI is looking for a scientist to uncover how Arctic sea-ice predictability evolves in a warming climate and to pioneer AI-enhanced approaches that advance our ability to predict sea-ice conditions from seasonal to multi-annual timescales.




The Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) opens a 4-year, full time position for a post doc research scientist in the Danish National Centre for Climate Research (NCKF), to work with AI-facilitated climate predictions of a seasonally ice-free Arctic in the Novo Nordic Foundation project IcyAlert (https://icyalert.github.io/).




IcyAlert (Intelligent Climate Early Warning Alert for Arctic Ice-Free Summers) is a research project funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation (NNF). The project goal is to improve predictions of Arctic ice-free summers and its potential climate impacts at multi-seasonal time scale using global climate models, causal analysis and machine learning. IcyAlert is led by DMI, in partnership with the Royal Meteorological Institute of Belgium (RMI) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU).




As part of NCKF at DMI, you will work in a research department with a strong profile in both global and regional climate modelling, as well as remote sensing. You will be part of the Global Climate unit in NCKF.




Your main tasks and responsibilities

In the IcyAlert project you will focus on how winter climate states and key physical drivers influence subsequent sea-ice evolution and predictability across seasonal to multi-annual timescales.




Building on causal relationships identified by RMI, you will use probabilistic AI methods to generate targeted initial-condition ensembles for sensitivity experiments.




You will then conduct and analyse both initialised ensemble prediction experiments for Arctic sea ice using the EC-Earth model system (https://ec-earth.org/), which is already running at DMI, to evaluate which winter variables or processes contribute most strongly to subsequent summer sea-ice predictability. The resulting process understanding and datasets will feed back into the ML-based, observation-driven Arctic sea-ice prediction system developed in collaboration with DTU.




You can expect to contribute to climate-impact assessments, including applications related to Arctic navigability. You will lead and co-author scientific publications and will contribute grant applications.




Your qualifications

We are particularly interested in candidates with a strong background in climate prediction, Arctic climate, and/or sea-ice science, as well as experience working with initialised ensemble prediction systems.

Expected qualifications include:




A PhD in climate science, atmospheric science, oceanography, sea-ice science, Earth-system science, applied mathematics, or a closely related field
Experience with initialised climate prediction systems, including ensemble-based forecasts or hindcast evaluation, and in working with large climate datasets
Strong scientific programming skills, particularly in Python, and preferably experience working with HPC environments
Good communication skills in oral and written English and collaboration skills for working with scientists within DMI and across three project partner institutions. The postdoctoral researcher will play a key role in connecting climate dynamics and initialized ensemble prediction (DMI), with causal methods (RMI), and AI/ML-based prediction (DTU). This will help ensure that IcyAlert forecasts are not only skilful but also physically interpretable and dynamically consistent.




Advanced expertise in developing new machine-learning architectures is not required. More important is the ability to physically understand initialised climate predictions, evaluate whether forecast signals are meaningful, and work effectively with AI/ML and causal-analysis methods developed in the IcyAlert project.

Where relevant, the postdoctoral researcher may also contribute to coordinated multi-annual hindcast experiments, such as the CMIP7/DCPP-A protocol, when this aligns with IcyAlert priorities and EC-Earth climate prediction-system development at DMI.




Who are we?

The position is in the Danish National Centre for Climate Research (NCKF) at the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI), which employs approximately 80 climate scientists of which 25 are located in the Global Climate unit. The companion Centre for Weather Research at DMI employs researchers working with meteorology, oceanography and hydrology. We have a strong international profile, which is also reflected in the many nationalities employed and in the use of both English and Danish as working languages.




NCKF has been established with the purpose to conduct critical climate research for the Kingdom of Denmark (Denmark, Greenland and the Faroe Islands) and bring together climate knowledge, to form the basis for green transition and climate adaptation. The activities include assessments of observed and future climate change of the physical climate system, with focus on the Polar regions and on extreme weather and sea level around Denmark. Across the department, climate research builds on both global and regional modelling as well as observations from remote sensing, in-situ measurements and field work. NCKF also develops the Danish Climate Atlas (Klimaatlas) which contains detailed data about expected future changes in the climate of Denmark.




DMI is part of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities. As of December 1, 2026, DMI will merge with our sister agency, Danish Agency for Climate Data, to become “DMI, Maps and Basic Data”. DMI is the government's climate science advisor, creating and communicating knowledge about weather, climate and the sea to the Danish Realm. DMI's warnings, weather forecasts and services safeguard life and infrastructure and provide a basis for planning in a changing climate. We have approximately 350 employees, most of whom work at DMI’s headquarters at Sankt Kjelds Gård in Østerbro, Copenhagen. After the merge, the new organization will have more than 600 employees. 




Employment and Salary

Will be in accordance with Danish Law and Agreements, specifically the Collective Agreement for State-Employed Academics (AC-overenskomsten). It will be possible to negotiate an addition to the basic salary depending on your qualifications and experience. DMI offers a flexible working week of 37 hours including a paid lunch break, and six weeks of paid vacation annually. If you come from abroad, there is a possibility for a reduced tax scheme the first 7 years in Denmark.




The position is a full-time position, limited to a duration of 4 years.




For further details about the position, please contact the Head of Global Climate unit, Ole Krarup Leth, at +45 23 82 72 23 or by e-mail at okl@dmi.dk or senior scientist and IcyAlert project leader Tian Tian at+45 24 81 32 03 or by e-mail tian@dmi.dk .




Apply now 

Please enclose a cover letter, a curriculum vitae (incl. publication list) and contacts for relevant professional references. Please note that applications may be shared with relevant project partners from DTU and RMI as a part of the recruitment process.

At DMI, diversity is an important value to us because we believe that an inclusive, versatile work environment strengthens task fulfilment. We actively work to foster diversity in our employee composition, reflected in our inclusive workplace and a balance between work and family life. We encourage everyone to apply for the position regardless of age, gender, sexuality, religion or ethnicity.




To apply for the position, please use the official link and follow the instructions.

Title: Scientific Data Architect - Austria, Denmark or UK
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
About TetraScience

TetraScience is the Scientific Data and AI Company building Tetra OS, the operating system for scientific intelligence. We help the world's leading life sciences firms turn fragmented scientific data into AI-native assets and scientific workflows that accelerate discovery, development, and manufacturing. TetraScience's growing ecosystem of strategic partners includes NVIDIA, Databricks, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Snowflake, Google, and Microsoft.

In connection with your candidacy, you will be asked to carefully review "The Tetra Way," authored by our CEO, Patrick Grady; it is impossible to overstate the importance of this document, and you should take it literally as you decide whether our mission, culture, and expectations are right for you.


Who You Are

You are a product-minded, outcome-obsessed driver of technical scientific solutions.

You a high velocity self-starter. You refuse to let uncertainty obstruct your path to designing and building solutions.

You roll up your sleeves, try things out, and get things done. You do not hesitate to prototype, demo, and build in order to accelerate delivery of products for your end users.

You thrive in environments where you can collaborate with scientists, product managers, and engineers to transform complex scientific data into actionable outcomes. Your ability to engage with scientists and business leaders alike makes you a key player in maximizing the value of scientific data.

With rich experience applying cutting edge data methodologies to the biopharma R&D domain, you bridge understanding between present-day pain points and generalizable solutions.

You are an insatiable learner, with a track record of deeply learning new tools, methods, and domains.

You fundamentally embody the principles of extreme ownership and have a demonstrated history of building extensible data models and applications for Biopharma end users to maximize value from their data via analysis and integration with AI/ML.

This role will require extreme self-discipline and determination as we forge a category that will fundamentally and forever change the life science industry.


What You Have Done


PhD with +4 years or Masters with +8 years of industry experience in life sciences  with extensive domain knowledge in drug discovery (target ID through lead optimization), preclinical development, CMC (all drug modalities), or product quality testing
Proven track record of defining, designing, prototyping, and implementing productized AI/ML-driven use cases in cloud environments
Collaborated with cross-functional teams, including product managers, software engineers, and scientific stakeholders
Performed extensive exploratory data analysis and workflow optimization to enable scientific outcomes not previously possible
Engaged diverse audiences, from scientists to executive stakeholders using your excellent communication and storytelling abilities
Advised scientists in a consulting capacity to further research, development, and quality testing outcomes


Requirements

What You Will Do



You will be a critical team member in a unique partnership to industrialize Scientific AI. As such, you will engage directly with customers onsite and will need to travel up to 25% of your time, building strong relationships, deeply understanding their scientific data challenges and requirements, and accelerating solutions
Design and implement extensible, reusable data models that efficiently capture and organize scientific data for scientific use cases, ensuring scalability and future adaptability
Translate scientific data workflows into robust solutions leveraging the Tetra Data Platform
Own, scope, prototype, and implement solutions including:
Data model design (tabular & JSON)
Python-based parser development
Lab software (e.g., ELN/LIMS) integration via APIs
Data visualization and app development in Python (using app frameworks like Streamlit and plotting tools like holoviews and Plotly) 
Collaborate with Scientific Business Analysts (SBAs), customer scientists and applied AI engineers to develop and deploy models (ML, AI, mechanistic, statistical, hybrid)
Programmatically interrogating proprietary instrument output files
Dynamically iterate with scientific end users and technical stakeholders to rapidly drive solution development and adoption through regular demos and meetings
Proactively communicate implementation progress and deliver demos to customer stakeholders
Collaborate with the product team to build and prioritize our roadmap by understanding customers' pain points within and outside Tetra Data Platform
Rapidly learn new technologies (e.g., new AWS services or scientific analysis applications) to develop and troubleshoot use cases


Benefits



Competitive Salary and equity in a fast-growing company
Supportive, team-oriented culture of continuous improvement
Generous paid time off (PTO)
Flexible working arrangements - Remote work when not at Customer Sites


We are not currently providing visa sponsorship for this position.

Title: Working in power markets? Let's talk
Place: Copenhagen Municipality, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Electricity Maps is building the world's most comprehensive electricity data platform. Real-time, historical, and forecasted electricity mix, prices, load, and carbon intensity across markets worldwide.

Power markets are a wide, fast-moving space and one with a lot of room for someone with the right experience to help shape what direction we take. That's why we'd rather meet you now even if we don't have an official role on the page. From there, we can figure out together what makes sense. We especially love hearing from people who come with a view: where you'd add value, what you'd want to work on or what you think we're missing.

Maybe you work in one of the following areas:


Day-ahead and intraday forecasting
BESS and asset optimization
Imbalance and balancing markets
Renewable generation forecasting (wind, solar, etc.)
Power market analytics or trading
Something adjacent


We're interested in talking across all lines of work in these areas: Engineering, ML, product, commercial, analytics, or something else. Whatever angle you come at it from, we're curious to hear it.

What to expect

We read every intro that comes through. If we see something we want to learn more about, we'll reach out to get to know each other and figure out together where your experience could add the most value.

About Electricity Maps

There are two sides to what we do. The first: decarbonizing the grid by making historical, real-time, and forecasted data on electricity mix, load, and carbon intensity available to anyone making smarter decisions across the energy transition.

The second is newer for us - we've started working with energy traders, asset operators, and BESS players in European power markets, building out price forecasting, market signals, and adjacent tooling. It's an area we're growing fast in and one with plenty of room for the right person to help shape where it goes.

The details


Location: Copenhagen (in-office with flexibility)
Compensation: Competitive salary + stock options (when a role materializes)
Benefits: 6 weeks vacation, health insurance, annual company offsite, lunch and snacks at office

Description:
Klarna, briefly

At Klarna, we're building an everyday finance network, helping over 120 million consumers across 26 countries save time and money, and worry less about their finances.Working at Klarna means taking on problems most companies never get to solve, and being hands-on enough that the interesting part of the work lands with you, not someone else. You'll build with AI, not watch it happen.

This is the stretch zone. Come find out what you're capable of.

About The Role

Klarna is bringing its Fair Financing product live in Denmark. As a Senior Analyst on the credit decisioning team, you'll build and defend the underwriting policies that decide who gets credit in Denmark and on what terms, working from bureau data and models built specifically for the Danish market.

You'll work alongside Product, Risk, and the regional Belgium team to bring that policy onto Klarna's Global Underwriting Platform (GUP), the shared framework that will power credit decisions across markets.

What You'll Do


You'll analyze consumer credit risk using SQL and Danish credit bureau data to find where underwriting policy should tighten or loosen.
You'll work with Product, Risk, and the Danish regional team to bring Denmark’s credit policy onto Klarna's Global Underwriting Platform.
You'll align purchase power and pre-qualification logic for the Danish market across Klarna's App and its One Card product.
You'll monitor how the Danish bureau data feeding your models performs, and flag where sourcing or model quality needs to change.
You'll turn what your analysis shows into policy changes that underwriting, product, and the regional team can act on directly.


Who you are


You've worked in consumer credit risk, underwriting, or credit policy, and you understand how a policy change affects both approval rates and portfolio health.
You're proficient in SQL and comfortable working directly with large, messy datasets.
You know credit bureau data, repayment behavior, and credit risk modeling well enough to spot where the numbers don't add up.
You work through ambiguous or inconsistent policy logic methodically until you find the actual root cause.
You can turn a data finding into a policy change that underwriting, product, and regional teams can each act on.


Bonus points for


A degree in Finance, Economics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.


Things you should know before applying


Working together: we value co-located teams; most teams currently meet in the office 2–3 days per week, and this varies by team and can change over time.
Non-obvious backgrounds are welcome. Diversity of skills, perspectives and backgrounds is how we create, innovate, and disrupt like no other.
Final compensation will be based on the candidate's qualifications, skills, and experience.
Depending on your background, this could land as an Analyst role or a Data Scientist role — we'll settle the exact title with you once we understand your experience.


Please include a CV in English.

Curious to learn more about Klarna and what it’s like to work here? Explore our career site.

Title: Postdoc in Large Language Models and Agentic AI for Pathogen Analysis - DTU Food
Place: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Job Description

Join an international effort to build an AI-powered infrastructure for global pathogen surveillance. The Global Pathogen Analysis Platform (GPAP), supported by up to DKK 200 million from the Novo Nordisk Foundation , brings together DTU, the University of Copenhagen, Statens Serum Institut and Imperial College London, alongside collaborators across Europe, Africa, Asia and the Americas. GPAP is developing a freely accessible platform combining advanced bioinformatics, AI agents and secure data collaboration to support infectious disease surveillance across human, animal and environmental health. Its mission is to give researchers and public health teams in low, middle and high-income countries the tools to analyze their data locally and act on the results.

We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher in large language models and agentic AI to join GPAP’s AI Research Team at DTU National Food Institute. You will develop multimodal models, investigate LLM post-training and build agents that connect scientific metadata with pathogen analysis workflows. The role combines methodological research with software development: you will lead projects, publish in leading scientific and AI venues and integrate your methods into an international research infrastructure being developed with the scientists and public health professionals who will use it.

Responsibilities And Qualifications

You will join as a senior technical member of the AI Research Team within GPAP. A central project will reduce the manual preparation needed before users can analyze their data, by automatically organizing metadata and matching it to the relevant samples and datasets. This metadata often arrives in inconsistent formats, scattered across spreadsheets, PDFs, images, webpages, notes and scripts. You will develop multimodal LLMs and coding agents that automatically extract and standardize this information, then match it to the corresponding samples and datasets uploaded by users or already available on GPAP. Alongside this project, you will also contribute to LLM post-training and agent development for pathogen analysis, working closely with Dr Harrison Bo Hua Zhu, Professor Samir Bhatt (University of Copenhagen and Imperial College London), Professor Frank Møller Aarestrup, and GPAP researchers and engineers.

Your main tasks will be to:


Develop multimodal LLMs and agents capable of writing and executing code to extract and organize metadata.
Collect examples from GPAP partners and through AI-assisted research, curate training data, and build benchmarks for metadata identification.
Investigate LLM post-training, including agentic reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation methods, for metadata processing and scientific analysis.
Build agent environments that connect models with bioinformatics pipelines, databases and scientific software, and integrate them into GPAP’s agentic AI service.
Evaluate agents for pathogen analysis, interpretation and scientific reporting, with attention to reproducibility and traceability.
Lead research and software development projects involving MSc and PhD students and other postdoctoral researchers, coordinating planning, implementation, code reviews and delivery within an agile team.
Publish research in leading AI conferences and scientific journals and communicate to GPAP collaborators and partners across disciplines.


We are looking for:


A strong research background in computer science, machine learning or a closely related field.
An interest in AI for Science but bioinformatics background is not required.
Experience in LLM post-training and benchmarking/evaluation.
Experience building agent harnesses and the software environments used to run and evaluate them.
Strong Python programming and software engineering skills, including testing, version control and collaborative development.
Experience with CI/CD, LLM serving/infrastructure and/or distributed systems.
Excellent written and spoken English. The ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly in presentations and discussions with collaborators and partners across disciplines, including those without an AI background.
Relevant publications, research software and open-source contributions will be considered in the assessment.


As a formal qualification, you must hold a PhD degree (or equivalent).

We offer

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and terms of employment

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures .

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is full-time, with a starting date of 1 December 2026 (or according to mutual agreement).

You can read more about career paths at DTU here .

Further information

For further information about the research project and position, please contact Dr Harrison Bo Hua Zhu at habhuz@dtu.dk at DTU National Food Institute.

Read more at https://www.food.dtu.dk/english/research/genomic-epidemiology and for GPAP please visit https://gpap.global/ .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark .

Application procedure

Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 21 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:


Application (cover letter)
CV
Academic Diplomas (MSc/PhD – in English)
List of publications
In your cover letter, describe your experience with LLM post-training, evaluation and agent development, and the research questions you would like to pursue within GPAP. Where available, include links to relevant software or other research outputs in your CV.


Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU National Food Institute

DTU National Food Institute conducts research into and disseminates - through advice, innovation and teaching - sustainable and value-creating solutions in the area of food and health for the benefit of society. The vision is to make a difference by generating future prosperity through research into food and health. The institute works to prevent disease and promote health, develop new and better food products for a growing population and create sustainable technological solutions, including biosolutions. The institute’s tasks are carried out in interdisciplinary collaboration within e.g. nutrition, chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, epidemiology, modelling, and technology. This is achieved through a strong academic environment of international top class with correspondingly skilled researchers and employees. The Institute employs approximately 390 staff members.

The DTU National Food Institute conducts research, education and scientific advisory work in food and health. GPAP brings together researchers in AI, bioinformatics, pathogen genomics and public health to make advanced analysis tools accessible to scientists and public health authorities worldwide. You will work within a collaboration involving DTU, the University of Copenhagen, Statens Serum Institut, Imperial College London and international partners.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Title: AI Engineer, Novonesis, Bagsværd
Place: Gladsaxe, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Interested in a career that matters?

At Novonesis, we believe biology holds the key to solving some of the world's biggest challenges. To accelerate this mission, we are strengthening our digital and AI capabilities across Product & Process Development (PPD).

You will join the newly formed Digital Enablement Team within PPD, an organization of more than 400 employees across six director areas and more than 10 geographical locations. The team brings together expertise in digital implementation, data engineering, AI and the wider PPD data landscape to support scientists and business functions across the organization.

Together, we will build a strong digital foundation, establish new ways of working and create practical solutions that help scientists work more efficiently and effectively. By partnering closely with local digital teams, scientists and platform experts, we enable the adoption of scalable digital and AI solutions that create value across PPD.

The role & your impact

As an AI Engineer, you will develop and implement AI-enabled scientific workflows that help transform how research and development is conducted across Novonesis. This role combines hands-on execution with innovation, requiring both strong technical capabilities and close collaboration with scientific stakeholders. You will play a key role in translating scientific challenges into practical AI solutions that are scalable, maintainable and aligned with Novonesis enterprise platforms and data foundations.

Your Key Responsibilities In This Role


Build and implement AI-enabled scientific workflows that improve research activities and create measurable value for scientists.
Design and develop solutions using enterprise AI platforms, models, data foundations and reusable components.
Contribute to next-generation R&D initiatives that connect data, models, tools and AI capabilities into integrated end-to-end workflows.
Work closely with scientists and local digital teams to understand user needs and iteratively develop solutions that fit real-world scientific processes.
Support adoption, integration and lifecycle management of AI solutions to ensure long-term impact and sustainability.


What You'll Need To Be Successful In This Role


BSc or MSc degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Machine Learning, Bioinformatics, or a related technical or scientific discipline, combined with professional working proficiency in English.
Experience developing and implementing AI, machine learning, or LLM-enabled solutions in operational or user-facing environments.
Strong programming skills, preferably in Python, with practical experience working with models, APIs, data pipelines, and modern software development practices.
Experience taking AI solutions beyond proof-of-concept through testing, integration, deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management.
Ability to collaborate effectively with scientists, software specialists, data engineers, and platform teams to develop, validate, and operationalize AI solutions.


We are looking for someone who demonstrates:


Strong AI problem-solving and engineering judgment, with the ability to identify where AI creates meaningful value and build reliable, maintainable solutions that deliver lasting impact.
An experimental and learning-oriented mindset, using evidence, user feedback, and technical results to iteratively improve solutions and adapt approaches when needed.
Excellent collaboration, curiosity, and learning agility, working effectively across scientific and technical disciplines while continuously exploring new technologies and ways of working.


Additional Skills & Interests We Value

Experience working in scientific R&D or laboratory environments would be an advantage, as would hands-on experience with agentic AI, generative AI, and LLM-based workflows. Familiarity with enterprise AI platforms and large-scale AI implementations is beneficial, particularly when combined with an understanding of data platforms that support scientific and research operations. Candidates with an interest in applying emerging AI technologies to solve complex scientific challenges will thrive in this environment.

What We Offer You

This is an opportunity to help shape a newly established team at the intersection of science, data, and AI. You will work alongside talented colleagues across multiple disciplines while contributing to initiatives that have impact on a global R&D organization.

In this role, you will have a unique opportunity to influence how AI is applied within scientific research and development while collaborating closely with scientists, digital specialists, AI experts, and data engineers across Novonesis. You will be part of a collaborative environment focused on learning, innovation, and continuous improvement, with access to enterprise-scale platforms and capabilities that support your professional growth. As the team continues to evolve, you will also play an important role in defining new ways of working and establishing best practices for AI adoption across PPD.

Working conditions

The position is based in Bagsværd, Denmark, and operates within an office-first hybrid work model. Onsite collaboration plays an important role in understanding scientific workflows, building strong stakeholder relationships, and working closely with colleagues across the organization. At the same time, we offer flexibility to work from home when compatible with team and project needs. Limited travel may be required depending on project activities and stakeholder engagement.

Application deadline: 16 October 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Contact Information: For more information, please contact Christian Munk, PPD Digitalization Lead, at crmu@novonesis.com or +45 30 77 04 33.

Our purpose guides the way

In Novonesis, we know that solutions rooted in biology can help solve humanity’s biggest challenges. Since we began more than a century ago, this has been our guide. It’s how we've gotten so far. And it’s how we'll impact the future. Now, more than ever, the world needs change. And with biosolutions, the possibilities for transformation are endless. If our purpose resonates with you, we encourage you to apply.

Opportunities for everyone

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunity for all applicants. Therefore we ask you to apply without a cover letter or photo and instead include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

We make all employment decisions based on business needs and welcome candidates with a wide range of backgrounds, including ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, or veteran status.

Explore Other Openings

If this position isn’t the right fit, you may still find other opportunities with us. You’re welcome to explore open roles or create a job agent to stay connected with future opportunities at novonesis.com/Career

Description:
Product Data Insights Lead




Ballerup, DK, 2750




At KMD, we build digital solutions used by millions of people around the world. Our mission is to ensure that they are reliable, accessible, and efficient.




We believe that the future is what you make it. So a career at KMD is a career with purpose and freedom. One where you’ll have a direct hand in improving the lives of people, while being empowered with the resources and autonomy to shape the course of your own professional journey.

Do you want to turn complex insights into software that makes a real difference to millions of citizens?

Do you have a background in data research and a sharp analytical mind? Can you turn customer research, usage data and competitive signals into evidence that helps product managers act on the right thing at the right time, whether that's a new product or an improvement to an existing one? Title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
Place: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
Description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at Veo you will get to work on challenging problems and directly contribute to the value created by our AI-driven end-user products.

You will become part of our AI team, which comprises 20+ researchers and engineers responsible for all stages in the machine learning lifecycles across different projects - from scoping and defining data annotation tasks to modeling, validation, and deployment. You will take ownership of the direction and execution of your projects while collaborating closely with the rest of the team, exchanging feedback, and helping others improve and succeed.

We stay current with the latest research and continuously discuss concepts and ideas in recent papers to assess their relevance to our tasks and product-specific challenges.

We are looking for an ambitious, high-performing senior engineer or researcher with a strong track record of delivering real-world machine learning systems. You should bring the technical depth and judgment needed to make sound decisions in complex and sometimes ambiguous environments.

What you will do:


Train state-of-the-art machine learning models
Write efficient inference pipelines for cloud and edge
Define and supervise data annotation tasks
Improve evaluation schemes to increase understanding of model performance and shortcomings
Contribute to long-term planning and prioritization of tasks
Mentor colleagues and raise the technical bar through feedback, knowledge sharing, and collaboration


What you could bring:


MSc or PhD in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience
Extensive hands-on experience delivering real-world, large-scale machine learning projects
Strong coding and software engineering skills, with experience building maintainable production systems
Experience taking ownership of technically complex projects from concept to deployment
Sound technical judgment and the ability to navigate ambiguity and balance research, product, and engineering considerations
A rigorous and critical approach to examining details, assumptions, and results
Strong communication skills and the ability to influence technical direction across teams


Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.
